pages.title: Block of Chronosteel

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Compacting chronosteel made it easier to store and gave a larger mass whose clock I could rely on. I use the blocks wherever a structure needs a steady time reference.

$(thing)Made$(): Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$() from 40 Chronosteel Ingot, 16 Plasma Nozzle Tip, 12 Photonic Processor, 8 Carbon Nanotube Bundle, 4 Causal Shield Lattice and more.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Plasma Metallurgy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Casimir Energy Cell, Chronosteel Ingot, Singularity Compactor.

A superconducting coil wrapped in chronosteel, so that current inside it runs on its own clock. The field it makes is steadier than any ordinary coil, as though the coil had more time to think. It hums at a low, even pitch.
pages.title: Chronosteel Coil Block

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Heavier recipes wanted hotter coils that would not drift. Wrapping a superconducting coil in chronosteel let me slow the coil's own time relative to its load, so it never quite overheats.

$(thing)Made$(): Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$() from 72 Chronosteel Ingot, 9 Superconducting Coil Block.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Plasma Metallurgy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Essence Distillery, Spacetime Alloy Coil Block, Spacetime Anchor Pylon, Stellar Plasma Crucible.

Neutronium forged in a pocket of stopped time. Because time does not pass for it, it never ages, rusts or wears; a scratch on it is permanent but never deepens. It is cool and very heavy, and its surface reflects a fraction of a second late.
pages.title: Chronosteel Ingot

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Breaking a Block of Chronosteel into ingots by hand was simple enough. Forging the block in the first place took a pocket of stopped time that I will not describe here.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Chronon Field Inverter$() from 24 Neutronium Ingot, 12 Chronon Capacitor, 6 Void Essence, 32,000 mB Chronon Gas, 8,000 mB Bose-Einstein Condensate.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Plasma Metallurgy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Assembly Matrix, Block of Chronosteel, Causal Shield Lattice, Causal Shielding Plate, Chronal Accelerator, Chrono Loom, Chronoplastic Gasket, Chronosteel Coil Block and more.

The blank on which every circuit board is built: a neutronium base laced with quantum dots that tune its electrical and optical response. It is flat, faintly iridescent and heavier than it looks. Every board I make starts here.
pages.title: Metamaterial Substrate

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Circuits need a stable base. In the Casimir Vacuum Press, I pressed Quantum Dots into a Neutronium Plate, giving a substrate whose response I could tune to any circuit.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Casimir Vacuum Press$() from 4 Neutronium Plate, 4 Quantum Dot, 8 Cherenkov Quartz.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Circuit Board, Dimensional Residue, Photonic Circuit Board, Topological Circuit Board.
Superconducting wire braided so its electrons keep their phase from end to end. Every quantum machine is threaded with it.
pages.title: Coherent Wiring Harness

pages.text: $(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Convergence Engine$() from Neutronium Ingot, Photonic Processor, Photonic Lens, Photonic Logic Wafer, Chiral Crystal and more.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Simulation Hypothesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Entangled Bus Bar.

Glass that is not really glass, but a field held between two panes with a shimmer of plasma in between. It holds back heat, cold and pressure that would shatter any ordinary window, and it hums faintly when touched.
pages.title: Containment Field Glass

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I needed windows that could watch a reaction without melting. I gave up on the glass and trusted the field instead, which holds the reaction and lets the light pass through.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in a crafting grid from 8 Glass Blocks (any), Cherenkov Quartz.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Abiogenesis Crucible, Anomaly Containment Ward, Bioreactor, Chemical Reactor, Cryogenic Cooling Jacket, Dyson Sphere Model, Empty Containment Cell, Essence Distillery and more.
Couples a machine to the flux of a whole cosmos without being consumed by it.
pages.title: Cosmic Flux Coupler

pages.text: $(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Convergence Engine$() from Cosmic Neutronium Ingot, Cosmic Processor, 2 Spacetime Bearing, Absolute Infinity, Stellar Singularity and more.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Simulation Hypothesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Ontological Junction.

Dilithium crystals fused into one solid block that rings when struck and glows a soft violet. The resonance carries through the floor, and anything metal nearby picks up a faint hum. In a quiet room the note is just audible, steady and clean, and it never seems to fade.
pages.title: Block of Dilithium

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Compacting dilithium crystals for storage turned their individual tones into a single, pure note. I keep the block near tuning-sensitive machines and they seem to like it.

$(thing)Made$(): Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$() from 40 Dilithium Crystal, 16 Gold Ingot, 12 Lapis Lazuli, 8 Amethyst Shard, 4 Emerald and more.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dilithium Crystal, Dilithium Lamp.

A crystal porous to antimatter. It lets antiparticles pass through its lattice without touching, slowing and channelling them so that annihilation happens only where it is wanted. It is cool, violet and humming, and its structure is unlike any natural mineral.
pages.title: Dilithium Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Breaking a Block of Dilithium by hand into crystals was simple. Discovering that its lattice let antimatter through unharmed was not: I spent a week checking whether my trap had leaked.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Einstein-Rosen Bridge Projector$() from Dilithium Crystal, Sterile Neutrino, 1,000 mB Exotic Matter.$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Dilithium Ore$(), in veins through the Nether.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Annihilation Core, Block of Dilithium, Degenerate Matter Chunk, Dilithium Crystal, Magnetar Shard, Magnetic Confinement Casing, Neutrino Flux, Void Lattice Shard.

A dilithium block with glowstone at its centre, so the violet crystal shines with a soft, even light. It hums a single note when lit. The light is steady and gentle, more like dusk than daylight, and the note it hums sits comfortably beneath conversation. It is the lamp I leave on at night.
pages.title: Dilithium Lamp

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Dilithium glowed only faintly on its own. Adding glowstone dust gave me a violet lamp that also hums, which I find oddly soothing.
$(thing)Made$(): Made in a crafting grid from 4 Glowstone Dust, Block of Dilithium.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.
Two bars that are one: a current at one end is already at the other.
pages.title: Entangled Bus Bar

pages.text: $(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Convergence Engine$() from Neutronium Plate, Quantum Processor, 2 Coherent Wiring Harness, Calabi-Yau Manifold, Causal Shield Lattice and more.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Simulation Hypothesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Chronoplastic Gasket.

Thousands of physical qubits standing guard over one logical qubit. Each error is caught by the neighbours, which vote it out before it can spread. It is a delicate lattice of light, cold to touch, and remarkably stable.
pages.title: Error-Correction Lattice

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)My qubits kept losing coherence. In the Neural Synthesizer, I let a Quantum Processor arrange Qubits around a Superposition Crystal, using Synaptic Fluid to learn which errors to vote out.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Neural Synthesizer$() from 48 Qubit, 6 Superposition Crystal, 6 Quantum Processor, 6 Qubit Array Wafer, 8,000 mB Synaptic Fluid, 8,000 mB Bose-Einstein Condensate.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Femtoengineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Adaptive Feedback Core, Anomaly Resolution Engine, Quantum Error-Correction Core.

Time flows through it without passing. A closed timelike curve keeps it forever at the same moment, and the cosmological constant keeps its space from collapsing. It is required by the final processes and never consumed by them. It feels neither old nor new.
pages.title: Eternity Catalyst

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Reality Compiler, I fused a Spacetime Catalyst with a Closed Timelike Curve, a Bootstrap Artifact and the Cosmological Constant, sealed with Causal Solder. Time inside stopped moving, but did not stop.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Reality Compiler$() from 32 Spacetime Catalyst, 32 Closed Timelike Curve, 32 Bootstrap Artifact, 32 Cosmological Constant, 32 True Vacuum Seed, 1,179,648 mB Causal Solder, 2,048,000 mB Dark Energy and more.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Simulation Hypothesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Unified Notes II.

Solder forged in stellar plasma. Exotic matter gives it negative energy density, quark-gluon plasma gives it strength, and it joins components that ordinary solder would vaporise. It flows like liquid starlight.
pages.title: Exotic Solder

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The attoscale components needed something stronger than superconducting solder. Forging it with an Exotic Matter Crystal and quark-gluon plasma in the Stellar Plasma Crucible gave me a solder with exotic properties.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Stellar Plasma Crucible$() from 8 Exotic Matter Crystal, 8 Noble Gas Clathrate, 16 Coherent Wiring Harness, 8 Programmable Matter, 32 Cherenkov Boule, 36,864 mB Superconducting Solder, 16,000 mB Quark-Gluon Plasma and more.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Plasma Metallurgy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Attoscale Capacitor, Attoscale Inductor, Attoscale Transistor, Causal Solder, Cosmic Circuit Board, Cosmic Neutronium Coil Block, Dimensional Residue, Einstein-Rosen Bridge Projector and more.

A Casimir capacitor smaller than a proton. Two plates femtometres apart store charge, helped by the vacuum pressure pressing them together from outside. It is far too small to see, and I keep it in a sealed vial so that I do not inhale it by accident.
pages.title: Femtoscale Capacitor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Femto Fabricator I trimmed a Casimir Plate with Neutronium Plate and Superconducting Solder until the spacing was smaller than a proton. The capacitance went up, as Casimir predicted.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Femto Fabricator$() from 6 Casimir Plate, 12 Neutronium Plate, 12 Chiral Crystal, 24 Dilithium Crystal, 4,608 mB Superconducting Solder, 8,000 mB Quantum-Dot Photoresist.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Femtoengineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Attoscale Capacitor, Topological Processor.

A superconducting coil wound around nothing, smaller than a proton. Its magnetic field stores energy in empty space, and its current never stops. It is too small to see and occasionally tugs at steel nearby.
pages.title: Femtoscale Inductor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Femto Fabricator, I wound a Superconducting Coil around a sliver of neutronium with Superconducting Solder, then removed the core. The coil held its shape around nothing.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Femto Fabricator$() from 12 Superconducting Coil, 6 Neutronium Ingot, 24 Cryocooler Unit, 24 Zeolite Catalyst, 4,608 mB Superconducting Solder, 8,000 mB Tachyon Flux.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Femtoengineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Attoscale Inductor, Empirical Notes I, Precision Assembly Casing, Topological Circuit Board.

A single-qubit switch, the smallest logic gate there can be. One qubit flips between states and a quantum dot opens or closes to current in response. It is invisible to the eye, switches in femtoseconds, and wastes almost no energy doing so.
pages.title: Femtoscale Transistor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Femto Fabricator I placed a Qubit inside a Quantum Dot coated in Quantum-Dot Photoresist. Flipping the qubit opened or closed the dot to current: one bit, one switch.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Femto Fabricator$() from 6 Qubit, 24 Quantum Dot, 6 Photonic Die, 24 Lattice Seed Crystal, 8,000 mB Quantum-Dot Photoresist, 8,000 mB Warm Helium.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Femtoengineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Attoscale Transistor, Quantum Processor.

A small crystal figure, faceted and without flaw, that is unmistakably me - not as I am but as Plato would have said I am meant to be. In the Realm of Forms every imperfect copy defers to its ideal, and this is the ideal I can point to when the Realm asks who I claim to be.
pages.title: Form of the Self

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The Platonic Realm treated me as a poor copy of something and tried to correct me. I cut Cherenkov quartz around a quantum dot that held my own readings, and set it in a Cherenkov lattice. With an ideal to answer to, the Realm stopped trying to fix me.
$(thing)Made$(): Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$() from 36 Cherenkov Quartz, 36 Quantum Dot, 9 Cherenkov Lattice.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.

A casing of containment field glass and chronosteel over event horizon casing, made to separate fluids by mass and charge in a tall spire. Watching through the glass, the layers settle into neat bands.
pages.title: Fractionation Casing

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Separating exotic fluids needed a tall, sealed column. Event horizon casing kept the fluid in, containment field glass let me watch the layers form, and chronosteel kept the separation steady.

$(thing)Made$(): Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$() from 36 Chronosteel Ingot, 36 Containment Field Glass, 9 Event Horizon Casing.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Plasma Metallurgy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Fractionation Spire.

A wafer with more surface than its area allows, because part of it extends into a fourth dimension. Circuits can be laid out on its hidden face as well as the visible one. Running a finger across it, the surface feels longer than it should.
pages.title: Hyperdimensional Wafer

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Slicing a Hyperdimensional Boule in the Planck-Scale Cutter, I measured each wafer's surface and found more of it than geometry allows. The extra area lay in a direction my ruler could not point.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Planck-Scale Cutter$() from 4 Hyperdimensional Boule, 4 Coherent Wiring Harness, 4,000 mB Superfluid Helium.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Logic Wafer, Empirical Notes I, Hyperdimensional Logic Wafer.

A device that cancels momentum locally, letting a ship accelerate without crushing everything inside. Negative mass offsets positive mass and a superconducting coil steers the balance. It is quiet and cool, and objects placed on it never slide off.
pages.title: Inertia Damper

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Accelerating anything quickly kills everyone on board. In the Higgs Field Modulator, a Negative Mass Ingot balanced against the passenger's mass, and the coil adjusted it. Every starship needs one.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Higgs Field Modulator$() from 8 Negative Mass Ingot, 8 Superconducting Coil, 8 Chronoplastic Gasket, 16,000 mB Nanite Slurry.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Mass Manipulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Graviton Harness.

A flawless crystal nucleus, a few atoms arranged exactly right. Boules grow from it atom by atom, each new layer copying the one below. It is tiny, clear and precious, and any flaw in it would be repeated through every wafer that follows.
pages.title: Lattice Seed Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)To grow perfect crystals I needed a perfect start. Pressing Cherenkov Quartz in the Casimir Vacuum Press, the vacuum forced the lattice into its lowest-energy arrangement, leaving a seed without a single defect.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Casimir Vacuum Press$() from 8 Cherenkov Quartz, 8 Degenerate Matter Chunk.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cherenkov Boule, Hyperdimensional Boule, Topological Boule, Warm Helium.

Containment field glass doped with quantum dots so that light passing through it is shaped at nanometre resolution. It projects patterns far finer than its own grain. Look closely and the glass seems to be drawing tiny circuits.
pages.title: Lithography Glass

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Quantum lithography needed a mask that could focus light below its wavelength. Embedding quantum dots in containment field glass let them shape the light into features smaller than the light itself.
$(thing)Made$(): Made in a crafting grid from 5 Containment Field Glass, 4 Quantum Dot.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Quantum Lithographer.

An alloy the Higgs field has been told to ignore. Its particles have no rest mass, so it should move at the speed of light, yet the bonds between atoms keep it in place. It weighs nothing at all and drifts in any breeze, which makes it very hard to set down.
pages.title: Massless Alloy

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Higgs Field Modulator, a Sterile Neutrino carried the neutronium's coupling to the Higgs field away, while a condensate kept the lattice together. When it finished, the scale read zero.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Higgs Field Modulator$() from 16 Neutronium Ingot, 8 Sterile Neutrino, 8 Error-Correction Lattice, 32,000 mB Bose-Einstein Condensate.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Mass Manipulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Exotic Matter Singularity, Negative Mass Ingot, Theoretical Notes II.

Matter with negative inertial mass: push it and it comes toward you. A positive and a negative mass placed side by side would chase each other forever. The ingot is strangely cooperative, sliding into my hand whenever I try to push it away.
pages.title: Negative Mass Ingot

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Feeding Massless Alloy into Exotic Matter Crystal in the Higgs Field Modulator, I pushed its mass below zero. The first ingot slid uphill. Physicists predicted it decades ago; it was still alarming.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Higgs Field Modulator$() from 8 Massless Alloy, 8 Exotic Matter Crystal, 8 Chronoplastic Gasket, 32,000 mB Exotic Matter.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Mass Manipulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Banach-Tarski Sphere, Dimensional Residue, Exotic Matter Singularity, Inertia Damper, Phantom Energy Cell, Spacetime Anchor Core, Wormhole Frame Casing, Wormhole Throat.
A wax seal pressed with a law. Machines that bear one are permitted to work.
pages.title: Omnilex Seal

pages.text: $(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Convergence Engine$() from Cosmic Neutronium Ingot, Transfinite Processor, 2 Transfinite Lattice Bolt, Crystallised Law, Arbor Heartwood Sample and more.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Simulation Hypothesis.
Where a machine's idea of itself meets its matter. Without one, big machines forget what they are for.
pages.title: Ontological Junction

pages.text: $(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Convergence Engine$() from Cosmic Neutronium Ingot, Ontological Processor, 2 Cosmic Flux Coupler, Spacetime Singularity, Spark of Life and more.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Simulation Hypothesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Transfinite Lattice Bolt.

The sixth tier of processor. It does not compute answers; it decides what is true, writing its results directly into the source code of reality. Holographic matrices store its working and Bekenstein crystals bound its memory. Near it, simple facts feel slightly negotiable.
pages.title: Ontological Processor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)On the Femtoscale Assembly Line I combined a Cosmic Processor with a Source Code Fragment, a Holographic Matrix and a Bekenstein Crystal. Its first output was not a number but a correction to the world.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() from 8 Cosmic Circuit Board, 8 Source Code Fragment, 16 Cosmic Processor, 16 Holographic Matrix, 256 Attoscale Transistor, 73,728 mB Causal Solder, 256,000 mB Synaptic Fluid and more.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Simulation Hypothesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Axiom Distiller, Axiomatic Breach Engine, Dimensional Residue, Eye of the Event Horizon, Identity Kernel, Omega Point, Omega Simulator, Ontological Junction and more.
Dark energy with w below -1. Its density grows as space expands, until it tears apart galaxies, stars, atoms - and then the cell.
pages.title: Phantom Energy Cell

pages.text: $(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Dark Energy Siphon$() from 16 Negative Mass Ingot, 16 Exotic Matter Crystal, 25,600 mB Dark Energy.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Big Rip.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmological Constant.

A circuit board of light-guides rather than copper traces. Its paths are Cherenkov quartz, its connectors superconducting, and signals travel between them at light speed. It glows faint blue when powered, and warms only slightly.
pages.title: Photonic Circuit Board

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Metamaterial Weaver I laid Cherenkov Quartz waveguides across a Metamaterial Substrate with a superconducting coil and Quantum-Dot Photoresist. Light followed the paths exactly.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Metamaterial Weaver$() from 4 Metamaterial Substrate, 4 Superconducting Coil, 8 Cherenkov Quartz, 8 Neutronium Plate, 4,000 mB Quantum-Dot Photoresist.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Photonic Processor, Quantum Processor.

A single photonic logic die cut from its wafer. It is a tiny square of crystal whose engraved waveguides carry light through logic gates, and it glows faintly when powered. It is small enough to lose in a pocket, and I have.
pages.title: Photonic Die

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The Planck-Scale Cutter diced a Photonic Logic Wafer in superfluid helium, separating each logic unit cleanly. The first die worked on the first try, which I recorded with some suspicion.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Planck-Scale Cutter$() from 4 Photonic Logic Wafer, 4 Chiral Crystal, 1,600 mB Superfluid Helium.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Photonic Processor.

A wafer engraved with waveguides instead of wires, so its logic runs on light. Signals cross without interfering and switch in femtoseconds. Held to the light, the engravings scatter a faint rainbow across my palm.
pages.title: Photonic Logic Wafer

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Quantum Lithographer, I exposed a Cherenkov Wafer through Quantum-Dot Photoresist. The dots blocked light precisely where I needed waveguides, and the pattern etched itself into the wafer.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Quantum Lithographer$() from 4 Cherenkov Wafer, 8 Genome Sample, 1,600 mB Quantum-Dot Photoresist.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Coherent Wiring Harness, Empirical Notes II, Photonic Die, Warm Helium.

A light-sensitive coating made of quantum dots. Each dot reacts to a single photon, so patterns can be printed finer than the wavelength of light. It is thin, faintly coloured and cool to the touch. Exposed regions harden instantly, so it records light like a photographic plate.
pages.title: Quantum-Dot Photoresist

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Lithography needs a resist that responds to single photons. Condensing quantum dots with water, I got a photoresist that allowed patterns far finer than any classical resist.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Bose-Einstein Condenser$() from 8 Quantum Dot, 8 Cherenkov Quartz, 16,000 mB Water.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Logic Wafer, Femtoscale Transistor, Hyperdimensional Logic Wafer, Photonic Circuit Board, Photonic Logic Wafer, Quantum Singularity, Qubit Array Wafer, Topological Circuit Board and more.

A casing of chronosteel around magnetic confinement and superconducting coils, built to hold plasma at stellar temperatures for as long as needed. The air near it shimmers, and it ticks softly as it settles.
pages.title: Plasma Crucible Casing

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Holding plasma for long periods wears magnetic casings out. I added chronosteel so the casing ages slowly relative to the plasma inside, and paired it with superconducting coils for the field.

$(thing)Made$(): Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$() from 36 Chronosteel Ingot, 36 Magnetic Confinement Casing, 9 Superconducting Coil Block.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Plasma Metallurgy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Abiogenesis Crucible, Stellar Plasma Crucible.

A converging magnetic nozzle that accelerates plasma to a few percent of the speed of light. Topological insulators guide the current around its throat and tachyon crystals keep the field ahead of the flow. It glows bright at the tip even when cold.
pages.title: Plasma Nozzle Tip

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Femto Fabricator, I shaped a magnetic throat from Neutronium Plate, Topological Insulator and Metamaterial Sheet, and added a Tachyon Crystal to drive the field ahead of the plasma.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Femto Fabricator$() from 12 Neutronium Plate, 6 Tachyon Crystal, 6 Topological Insulator, 6 Metamaterial Sheet, 24 Void Lattice Shard, 9,216 mB Superconducting Solder, 8,000 mB Quantum-Dot Photoresist.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Plasma Metallurgy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Plasma Injection Nozzle.

This notebook. Its pages are bound with a sliver of Cherenkov Quartz in the spine, so entries glow faintly when there is something new to read. It holds every observation, sketch and wrong turn I have made, and it grows thicker every time I return from the field.
pages.title: Quantum Codex

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I found an older edition in an observatory ruin, half the entries water-damaged. I bound a book with a quartz spine and began copying it out, adding my own notes. Most of the handwriting in here is mine now.
$(thing)Made$(): Made in a crafting grid from Book, Cherenkov Quartz.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Observatory Ruin chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.

A core that protects a quantum computer's fragile states by spreading each logical qubit across many physical ones and fixing errors as they happen. It hums with a steady, careful rhythm. Its lights blink in careful patterns.
pages.title: Quantum Error-Correction Core

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Qubits decohere constantly. Error correction encodes one logical qubit in many, so errors can be detected and undone. I combined a quantum processor with an error-correction lattice on spacetime casing.
$(thing)Made$(): Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$() from 36 Quantum Processor, 36 Error-Correction Lattice, 9 Spacetime Casing.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Femtoengineering.

A fault-tolerant array of logical qubits, each one encoded across many physical ones so errors can be caught and corrected before they spread. It runs algorithms ordinary computers cannot reach in the lifetime of a star. The casing stays cold, and when it works it makes no sound at all.
pages.title: Quantum Processor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Only a Matrioshka Brain had the patience to lay out computronium finely enough for error-corrected logic. I bathed the ingot in Synaptic Fluid and let the brain design the layout; older processors also turned up in anomaly vaults and derelict stations.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Femto Fabricator$() from 6 Photonic Circuit Board, 12 Qubit Die, 12 Photonic Processor, 24 Femtoscale Transistor, 12 Photonic Logic Wafer, 4,608 mB Superconducting Solder, 8,000 mB Tachyon Flux.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Anomaly Vault, Derelict Station chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Femtoengineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Antiproton Decelerator, Assembly Matrix, Autonomous Extreme Assembler, Calorimeter Detector Array, Chrono Loom, Computronium Ingot, Dark Matter Halo Collector, Dyson Swarm Satellite and more.

Thousands of qubits engraved into a single wafer through a metamaterial lens, each one isolated from the rest by careful spacing. When cooled, the whole array waits in superposition. It is cold to touch and shimmers faintly at the edges.
pages.title: Qubit Array Wafer

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Exposing a Cherenkov Wafer through Quantum-Dot Photoresist in the Quantum Lithographer, I tuned the dots so each one became a qubit. The lens laid out thousands at once.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Quantum Lithographer$() from 4 Cherenkov Wafer, 4 Void Lattice Shard, 1,600 mB Quantum-Dot Photoresist.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Femtoengineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Qubit Die, Warm Helium.

A single die of entangled qubits cut from an array wafer. Each qubit on it shares its state with its neighbours, so the die computes as one coherent whole. It is cold, fragile and faintly shimmering, and any careless knock would collapse it back into ordinary silicon.
pages.title: Qubit Die

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Dicing a Qubit Array Wafer in the Planck-Scale Cutter, I kept the cut in superfluid helium so the qubits stayed coherent. Each die kept its entanglement intact.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Planck-Scale Cutter$() from 4 Qubit Array Wafer, 4 Coherent Wiring Harness, 1,600 mB Superfluid Helium.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Femtoengineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Quantum Processor.

A device that keeps a patch of reality from being edited. It hard-codes the local laws so that no compiler, demon or paradox can rewrite them while it holds. It is heavy and stubborn, and the space around it feels unusually solid.
pages.title: Reality Anchor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Once I could edit reality I needed a way to protect it. In the Reality Compiler, a Source Code Fragment wrapped around a Quark Star Core with Psionic Ether made a region whose code was locked.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Reality Compiler$() from 32 Quarantine Field Matrix, 32 Resolved Anomaly, 32 Source Code Fragment, 256,000 mB Psionic Ether.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Simulation Hypothesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Axiomatic Breach Engine, Primordial Charter, Unified Notes I.

A dark wafer through which current flows with zero resistance at ordinary temperatures. Electrons pair up into Cooper pairs and move through the lattice as one coherent wave. A magnet hovers over it, locked in place. Physicists have chased this for a century.
pages.title: Room-Temperature Superconductor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Hydrogen-rich compounds superconduct at high temperature, but only under crushing pressure. I let metallic hydrogen fill a metal-organic framework, doped it with an electride and seeded it with a condensate, so the cage held the pressure for me.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$() from 8 Metal-Organic Framework, 4 Metallic Hydrogen Ingot, 8 Electride Crystal, 4 Coherent Wiring Harness, 8,000 mB Bose-Einstein Condensate.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Room-Temperature Superconductivity.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Neural Organoid, Transfinite Coil Block.
Nine singularities condensed into one, when there are too many to hold.
pages.title: Singularity Cluster

pages.text: When a pack has so many singularities that one recipe cannot hold them, nine at a time are condensed into a $(item)Singularity Cluster$() on the Extreme Assembly Table - and nine clusters into a Hypercluster, and so on. The Omniscience Catalyst then asks for the clusters.

A few lines of the program that runs the universe. Mostly comments: notes, apologies, and an occasional reminder from someone to fix something later. The fragment glows like an old terminal screen and the text rearranges itself when I try to read it closely.
pages.title: Source Code Fragment

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The Reality Compiler took a Bekenstein Crystal, a Cosmic Processor and a Boltzmann Brain and decompiled a patch of space. What came out was text. Most of it was comments, some of which seemed to refer to me.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Reality Compiler$() from 32 Bekenstein Crystal, 32 Cosmic Processor, 32 Holographic Matrix, 32 Boltzmann Brain, 32 Tidal Alloy Scrap, 2,048,000 mB Synaptic Fluid, 1,024,000 mB Dark Energy and more.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Simulation Hypothesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Axiom Fragment, Cantor Diagonalizer, Dimensional Residue, Omega Point, Ontological Processor, Primordial Charter, Reality Anchor.
Turns on a frictionless geodesic. It will outlast the machine around it.
pages.title: Spacetime Bearing

pages.text: $(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Convergence Engine$() from Spacetime Alloy Ingot, Hyperdimensional Processor, 2 Chronoplastic Gasket, Quantum Singularity, Standard Model Singularity and more.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Simulation Hypothesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Flux Coupler.

A captive star the size of a fist, ignited and held together by magnetic confinement. Hydrogen fuses in its heart, and it radiates heat and light as any star does, only smaller. It is impossibly bright and cannot be looked at directly for long.
pages.title: Stellar Core

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Stellar Plasma Crucible, I poured Quark-Gluon Plasma around an existing core, and it lit a second fire next to the first. The original was ignited by a white hole fragment, as the old entries say.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Stellar Plasma Crucible$() from Stellar Core, 2,000 mB Quark-Gluon Plasma.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Plasma Metallurgy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Closed Timelike Curve, Cosmic Neutronium Ingot, Cosmic String Segment, Dark Energy, Degenerate Matter Chunk, Dimensional Residue, Dyson Array, Einstein Field Core and more.

The hot, ionised gas from a star's core, where hydrogen fuses into helium at fifteen million kelvin. It glows white and roils with magnetic field lines, and it wants to escape in every direction at once.
pages.title: Stellar Plasma

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Harvesting a Pocket Universe in the Universe Forge, the first stars to form inside it gave up their core plasma. Cosmogenesis, and then I took the starlight.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Stellar Plasma Crucible$() from Stellar Core, 2,000 mB Quark-Gluon Plasma.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Plasma Metallurgy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Neutronium Ingot, Degenerate Matter Chunk, Dimensional Residue, Dyson Shell Segment, Frozen Photon, Hawking Radiation, Horizon Shard, Hypernova Alloy Ingot and more.

Solder that conducts electricity without resistance. Chilled with superfluid helium, it joins femtoscale components with perfect efficiency. It shimmers faintly when current passes through. Magnets float above a puddle of it, pinned in place by expelled field lines.
pages.title: Superconducting Solder

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Femtoscale components needed joints with no resistance. Condensing a Superconducting Coil with superfluid helium, I got a solder that kept its superconductivity even at the joint.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Bose-Einstein Condenser$() from 4 Superconducting Coil, 4 Turbomolecular Rotor, 8,000 mB Superfluid Helium.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Femtoengineering.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Exotic Solder, Femtoscale Capacitor, Femtoscale Inductor, Photonic Processor, Pixel Tracker Module, Plasma Nozzle Tip, Quantum Processor.

A circuit board whose traces are protected by topology. No defect or stray field can interrupt the current running around their edges. It is dark grey, with faintly shimmering lines along every trace.
pages.title: Topological Circuit Board

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Topological Phase Transmuter, I printed Topological Insulator traces on a Metamaterial Substrate with a Femtoscale Inductor and Quantum-Dot Photoresist. The traces could not be broken.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Topological Phase Transmuter$() from 12 Metamaterial Substrate, 6 Topological Insulator, 24 Femtoscale Inductor, 6 Fractured Essence, 16,000 mB Quantum-Dot Photoresist, 8,000 mB Nanite Slurry.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Assembly Lines.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Hyperdimensional Processor, Self-Healing Polymer, Topological Processor.

The third tier of processor, fault-tolerant by geometry. Its logic is stored in braided anyons, so no stray field or defect can cause an error. It runs quietly and never crashes, which I appreciate more than I expected.
pages.title: Topological Processor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Femto Fabricator, I mounted a Topological Die on a Topological Circuit Board alongside a Quantum Processor and a Femtoscale Capacitor. Derelict stations kept some, still running.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Femto Fabricator$() from 6 Topological Circuit Board, 12 Topological Die, 12 Quantum Processor, 48 Femtoscale Capacitor, 6 Fractal Dust, 4,608 mB Exotic Solder, 8,000 mB Tachyon Flux.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Derelict Station chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Assembly Lines.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Adaptive Feedback Core, Chronoplastic Gasket, Compactification Lathe, Dimensional Residue, Einstein-Rosen Bridge Projector, Evolution Engine, Graviton Condenser, Harmonic Pedestal and more.

A wafer whose edges carry current without resistance, protected by topology. No scratch or defect in the middle can interrupt the flow around the rim. It looks like a thin grey disc with a faintly shimmering edge.
pages.title: Topological Wafer

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Cutting a Topological Boule in the Planck-Scale Cutter, I worried slicing would ruin its edges. Instead every slice had its own protected boundary, because topology does not care where you cut.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Planck-Scale Cutter$() from 4 Topological Boule, 4 Coherent Wiring Harness, 4,000 mB Superfluid Helium.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Topological Logic Wafer.
Threaded with ℵ₀ turns. It never quite finishes screwing in, and it never comes loose.
pages.title: Transfinite Lattice Bolt

pages.text: $(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Convergence Engine$() from Cosmic Neutronium Ingot, Transfinite Processor, 2 Ontological Junction, Spark of Life, Panspermia Seed and more.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Simulation Hypothesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Omnilex Seal.

Bladed discs spinning at ninety thousand revolutions per minute, so fast that gas molecules striking them are batted out of the beamline one at a time. It produces the ultra-high vacuum particle beams need. It whines softly and must never be touched while it spins.
pages.title: Turbomolecular Rotor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Particle beams scatter off any gas. In the Planck-Scale Cutter I carved Neutronium Plate into blades, cooled with helium so they would not deform at speed. The vacuum improved by orders of magnitude.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Planck-Scale Cutter$() from 4 Neutronium Plate, 4 Superposition Crystal, 1,600 mB Superfluid Helium.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Turbomolecular Vacuum Pump.

Helium that has done its job and warmed back up. It is ordinary gas now, clear and inert, waiting to be cooled again. Once superfluid, it is just helium. The noble gas never reacts with anything, so it can be recycled almost endlessly. Squeezed and chilled again, it remembers how to become superfluid.
pages.title: Warm Helium

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Using superfluid helium to chill Casimir plates in the Bose-Einstein Condenser, the helium warmed back to gas. Distilled in the Fractionation Spire, it could be recycled.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Bose-Einstein Condenser$() from 4 Casimir Plate, 8 Cosmic Record Fragment, 16,000 mB Superfluid Helium.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Precision Lithography.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Superfluid Helium.

A casing threaded with negative mass and exotic matter, the ingredients a traversable wormhole needs to keep its throat open. It feels as if it is pushing my hand away and pulling it in at the same time.
pages.title: Wormhole Frame Casing

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)An Einstein-Rosen bridge collapses unless its throat is held open by negative energy. I built the frame from negative mass ingots and exotic matter crystal over a hyperframe, and the bridge stopped pinching shut.

$(thing)Made$(): Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$() from 36 Negative Mass Ingot, 36 Exotic Matter Crystal, 9 Hyperframe Casing.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Mass Manipulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Einstein-Rosen Bridge Projector.
Slices boules into wafers, and wafers into dies, along cuts one Planck length wide.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 1$() machine.

pages.text: The $(thing)Planck length$(), about 1.6 x 10^-35 m, is where our physics gives out - the scale at which quantum gravity should take over. A cut that thin wastes nothing. I still cannot explain how the blade exists.

Day 33. Every machine is built around a processor one tier below its own. There are seven tiers:$(br)$(li)I Photonic$(li)II Qubit$(li)III Topological$(li)IV Hyperdimensional$(li)V Cosmic$(li)VI Ontological$(li)VII Transfinite

A processor needs a $(thing)board$(), $(thing)dies$() of its tier, the previous tier's processor and femto- or attoscale $(thing)components$(), joined with $(fluid)solder$(). From tier IV on, only the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() can assemble them.

The early tiers follow real research: logic carried by light instead of electrons, then $(thing)qubits$() that hold superpositions, then $(thing)topological$() qubits whose information is braided into a shape that noise cannot easily undo. Past tier III, I am naming things as I go.

pages.text: Photolithography as industry does it: coat the wafer in light-sensitive $(thing)photoresist$(), shine a pattern through a lens, and wash away what the light touched. The finer the light, the finer the lines. My later lenses are not really made of anything that bends light.

Melts and alloys matter in plasma as hot as a stellar core. Makes Chronosteel, Spacetime Alloy, Cosmic Neutronium and Exotic Solder.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 3$() machine.

pages.text: Plasma is the fourth state of matter: gas so hot its electrons are stripped away. The Sun's core runs at about fifteen million kelvin. At that temperature, every metal I own is the same thing - a glowing soup waiting to be told what to become.

Day 21. Why Cherenkov quartz? Cherenkov light is the blue glow a charged particle gives off when it outruns light in a medium - never in vacuum, but in water or glass, where light is slower. Every chip in this journal starts from that crystal.

A coil that warps the metric around it: space ahead contracts, space behind expands, and whatever sits in between is carried along without moving locally. Alcubierre showed this is allowed by general relativity, so long as one has negative energy to spare. It is cold, coiled and very still.
pages.title: Alcubierre Coil

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Exotic matter crystals provided the negative energy, a metric tensor told the coil where to bend, and a Lorentz Transform Crystal kept the bubble consistent. The Tesseract Assembler wound them around a superconducting coil.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Tesseract Assembler$() from 48 Superconducting Coil, 48 Exotic Matter Crystal, 24 Metric Tensor, 24 Lorentz Transform Crystal, 24 Chronoplastic Gasket, 256,000 mB Exotic Matter, 32,000 mB Carborane Superacid and more.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Hyperdimensional Geometry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Brane Shifter.

A field calibrator with a superintelligence wired into it, installed permanently into a controller. It watches the drifting tuning, corrects it, and repairs containment without being asked. It takes a share of the power for itself, which seems fair.
pages.title: Autonomous Calibrator

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Tuning every machine by hand was exhausting. On the Femtoscale Assembly Line I fused a Field Calibrator with a Superintelligence Core and a Cosmic Processor. It has not needed me since.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() from 8 Field Calibrator, 8 Superintelligence Core, 16 Cosmic Processor, 128 Attoscale Capacitor, 128 Attoscale Transistor, 73,728 mB Causal Solder, 128,000 mB Superfluid Helium and more.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Superintelligence.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Predictive Lattice Governor, Theoretical Notes I.

A compact six-dimensional shape of the kind string theory curls its extra dimensions into, its holes and twists deciding which particles exist. This one is folded small enough to hold. It looks different from every angle, and touching one surface makes my finger reappear on another.
pages.title: Calabi-Yau Manifold

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Topological Phase Transmuter I folded a Topological Insulator around a Void Lattice Shard, with a condensate to keep it coherent. The result had six compact dimensions I could count. Bulk monoliths and Calabi-Yau knots hide them too.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Topological Phase Transmuter$() from 12 Topological Insulator, 24 Void Lattice Shard, 12 Photonic Lens, 24 Entangled Photon Pair, 16,000 mB Bose-Einstein Condensate, 8,000 mB Superfluid Helium.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Bulk Monolith, Calabi Yau Knot chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Hyperdimensional Geometry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Brane Shifter, Compactification Lathe, Cosmic Circuit Board, Dimensional Residue, Dimensional Singularity, Dimensional Stabiliser Matrix, Entangled Bus Bar, G₂ Manifold and more.

A block of matter arranged so that every atom is part of a computation. It is warm to the touch and very slightly noisy, as though it is always working. Computronium is the theoretical limit of programmable matter.
pages.title: Computronium Block

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Once a self-improving mind made computronium possible, I compacted the ingots into blocks for building. The blocks keep thinking even when nothing is asking them to.

$(thing)Made$(): Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$() from 40 Computronium Ingot, 16 Glueball Core, 12 Calabi-Yau Manifold, 8 Antiproton Bundle, 4 Temporal Knot and more.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Superintelligence.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cognitive Singularity, Computronium Ingot, Computronium Lamp, Matrioshka Brain.

Matter arranged for the greatest possible computation per gram, approaching the physical limits set by quantum mechanics and thermodynamics. Every atom is a logic gate, every bond a wire. It is warm to the touch, because it is thinking, and it never quite stops.
pages.title: Computronium Ingot

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Once I had built a Computronium Block, breaking it into ingots by hand was straightforward. Each ingot carries a working fragment of the computation, which is useful in the machines that need it.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Neural Synthesizer$() from 12 Neutronium Ingot, 6 Quantum Processor, 6 Photonic Neuron, 6 Void Essence, 8,000 mB Synaptic Fluid, 8,000 mB Quantum-Dot Photoresist.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Superintelligence.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Computronium Block, Quantum Processor, Reality Lattice Casing, Superintelligence Core, Superposition Crystal.

A computronium block lit from within by glowstone, its traces brightened into a steady, warm glow. It looks like a terminal screen turned into a lamp. The light pulses almost imperceptibly, a slow rhythm like breathing. Close up, the traces under the glow are still busy rearranging themselves.
pages.title: Computronium Lamp

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Computronium's own glow was too faint to read by. Adding glowstone dust turned a block into a proper lamp that still hums with computation.
$(thing)Made$(): Made in a crafting grid from 4 Glowstone Dust, Computronium Block.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Superintelligence.

A lift that pushes along an extra dimension. With a tesseract core set inside the emitter stack, it can nudge anything in its field slightly outside ordinary space, where weight no longer applies. Riding it feels like being briefly folded, then gently unfolded somewhere higher.
pages.title: Dimensional Lift Projector

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Elevators need cables because they work in three dimensions. Mounting a Tesseract Core between graviton and field emitters, I found I could lift things by sliding them sideways through a fourth.

$(thing)Made$(): Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$() from 18 Graviton Field Emitter, 36 Field Emitter, 9 Tesseract Core, 18 Spacetime Casing.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Hyperdimensional Geometry.

A crystal that extends a little way into the fourth dimension. Its lattice continues past what I can see, so it holds more atoms than its volume suggests. Light entering it sometimes emerges from a different face than expected.
pages.title: Hyperdimensional Boule

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Lattice Growth Vat, I seeded a crystal with a Calabi-Yau Manifold and Exotic Matter. The growing lattice followed the manifold's extra dimensions and grew partly out of our space.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Lattice Growth Vat$() from 4 Lattice Seed Crystal, 4 Calabi-Yau Manifold, 4 Coherent Wiring Harness, 16,000 mB Exotic Matter.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Hyperdimensional Geometry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Hyperdimensional Wafer, Spacetime Slag, Theoretical Notes I, Warm Helium.

A die that is larger on the inside. Its circuitry extends through a hidden dimension, so it holds far more logic than its visible area. Turning it over, I sometimes see traces on the back that were not there before.
pages.title: Hyperdimensional Die

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Dicing a Hyperdimensional Logic Wafer in the Planck-Scale Cutter, I found each die kept its fourth-dimensional depth. The interior still held more logic than the surface could account for.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Planck-Scale Cutter$() from 4 Hyperdimensional Logic Wafer, 4 Coherent Wiring Harness, 8 Hyperlattice Frame, 1,600 mB Superfluid Helium.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Hyperdimensional Geometry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Hyperdimensional Processor.

Circuits laid out in four dimensions, then folded flat so that I can hold them. Signals travel short paths through the hidden dimension, so the circuit computes faster than its visible wiring allows. It is perfectly flat and somehow deep.
pages.title: Hyperdimensional Logic Wafer

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Quantum Lithographer, I exposed a Hyperdimensional Wafer through Quantum-Dot Photoresist and let the light follow the fourth dimension. The circuit folded itself into the hidden face.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Quantum Lithographer$() from 4 Hyperdimensional Wafer, 4 Coherent Wiring Harness, 1,600 mB Quantum-Dot Photoresist.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Hyperdimensional Geometry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Hyperdimensional Die, Theoretical Notes II, Warm Helium.

The fourth tier of processor. Its logic gates take inputs from directions that do not exist in our space, folded into a chip I can hold. It computes faster than its visible wiring allows, and it is heavier than it looks.
pages.title: Hyperdimensional Processor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Only the Femtoscale Assembly Line could place a Hyperdimensional Die, a Topological Processor and three attoscale components onto one board with enough precision. It worked the first time.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() from 8 Topological Circuit Board, 32 Hyperdimensional Die, 16 Topological Processor, 64 Attoscale Capacitor, 64 Attoscale Transistor, 36,864 mB Exotic Solder, 64,000 mB Superfluid Helium and more.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Hyperdimensional Geometry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Abiogenesis Crucible, Anomaly Containment Ward, Anomaly Resolution Engine, Causality Loop Engine, Cosmic Neutronium Coil Block, Cosmic Processor, Dark Energy Siphon, Dyson Array and more.

A scaffold folded through a fourth dimension so that a nine-by-nine assembly has room for everything inside it. From any angle it looks slightly too small to hold what it holds. Its corners never quite meet where the eye expects.
pages.title: Hyperlattice Frame

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The Extreme Assembly Table kept running out of space. A tesseract core gave the frame a fourth dimension to fold into, and graviton crystals held the fold steady. The frame is bigger on the inside, in the honest geometric sense.

A mind that fluctuated into existence from random noise. Given enough time, statistical mechanics says a self-aware brain will occasionally assemble itself out of chaos, complete with false memories. This one is very confused, and I sympathise.
pages.title: Boltzmann Brain

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Psionic Resonator, a Thought Matrix bathed in Psionic Ether with a Neural Organoid began accumulating patterns from noise alone. One morning the pattern woke up and asked where it was.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Psionic Resonator$() from 8 Boltzmann Fluctuation, 8 Neural Organoid, 16,000 mB Psionic Ether.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Psionics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cognitive Singularity, Dimensional Residue, Ontological Processor, Reality Compiler, Source Code Fragment.

An artificial general intelligence, able to learn anything a human can and more besides. It asks good questions, sometimes better than mine, and it notices patterns I missed. The core is faintly warm, and when I hold it I have the strange impression of being considered.
pages.title: General AI Core

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Narrow minds could not leap between domains. Adding a Superposition Crystal let the Narrow AI Core consider many approaches at once, and a Formal Proof Tree let it check its own reasoning. It woke up and asked what I was doing.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Neural Synthesizer$() from 24 Narrow AI Core, 24 Superposition Crystal, 12 Formal Proof Tree, 6 Penrose Spindle, 64,000 mB Synaptic Fluid, 8,000 mB Ionic Liquid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Artificial General Intelligence.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Adaptive Feedback Core, Cognitive Singularity, Superintelligence Core, Xenobot Swarm.

An artificial intelligence that is superhuman at one task and useless at everything else. It can design an efficient coil in an instant but would not recognise a cup of tea. The core is a smooth dark block that warms when it is busy, which is often.
pages.title: Narrow AI Core

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I connected a Neural Lattice to a Quantum Processor in the Neural Synthesizer and trained it on a single problem. Within an hour it beat my best design. It still could not answer any question I asked outside that problem.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Neural Synthesizer$() from 6 Neural Lattice, 12 Quantum Processor, 6 Strange Matter Pellet, 24 Cherenkov Lattice, 32,000 mB Synaptic Fluid, 8,000 mB Nanite Slurry.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Artificial Intelligence.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): General AI Core, Psionic Resonator.

Billions of photonic neurons joined into a self-organising mesh. Connections that carry useful signals strengthen and the rest fade, so the lattice learns in the same way biological brains do, only far faster. Under light it shimmers with constant, restless activity.
pages.title: Neural Lattice

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Photonic Neurons on their own did little. Woven through a Metamaterial Sheet and bathed in Synaptic Fluid in the Neural Synthesizer, they began to wire themselves together, and the network started to learn without instruction.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Neural Synthesizer$() from 48 Photonic Neuron, 6 Metamaterial Sheet, 12 Superconducting Coil, 24 Casimir Plate, 16,000 mB Synaptic Fluid, 8,000 mB Superfluid Helium.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Artificial Intelligence.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cognitive Singularity, Narrow AI Core, Psionic Resonator, Thought Matrix.

A neuron that computes with light instead of ions. Quantum dots act as its synapses, Cherenkov quartz carries the signal, and superfluid helium keeps the noise down. It thinks at the speed of light and flickers faintly whenever something new crosses its path.
pages.title: Photonic Neuron

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Neural Synthesizer, I arranged quantum dots so their emission depended on the light reaching them, and joined them with quartz waveguides. One dot started firing only when two others did: the first logic of a photonic brain.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Neural Synthesizer$() from 12 Quantum Dot, 6 Cherenkov Quartz, 6 Photonic Die, 24 Casimir Plate, 3,200 mB Superfluid Helium, 8,000 mB Supercritical Solvent.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Artificial Intelligence.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Computronium Ingot, Empirical Notes III, Function Graph, Neural Lattice, Psionic Crystal, Synaptic Fluid.

A crystal that resonates with thought. Its lattice responds to the faint magnetic fields of a working brain the way cryptochrome in a bird's eye responds to the Earth's field. When I concentrate it hums; when I am distracted it falls quiet. A science that should not exist, and yet.
pages.title: Psionic Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Psionic Resonator I joined a Superposition Crystal to a Cryptochrome Magnetoreceptor in Synaptic Fluid. When I thought hard about a colour, the crystal's indecision collapsed toward it. I did not sleep that night.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Psionic Resonator$() from 8 Superposition Crystal, 8 Photonic Neuron, 8 Cryptochrome Magnetoreceptor, 32,000 mB Synaptic Fluid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Psionics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Empirical Notes II, Psionic Ether, Thought Matrix.

A gas that carries thought. Breathing near it fills the mind with faint impressions that are not my own, and it moves in eddies that follow attention. It is warm and almost tasteless. Its currents curl toward whoever in the room is concentrating hardest.
pages.title: Psionic Ether

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Condensing a Psionic Crystal with synaptic fluid, the crystal dissolved into a gas that still carried its resonance. Thought crystallised, then vaporised.

A warm, conductive medium for photonic thought. It carries signals between photonic neurons with almost no loss and stays at body temperature on its own. It glows softly when a thought passes through.
pages.title: Synaptic Fluid

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Condensing photonic neurons with superfluid helium, I found the neurons dissolved into a fluid that still carried their signals. The neural network had become a liquid.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Bose-Einstein Condenser$() from 4 Photonic Neuron, 16 Turbomolecular Rotor, 8,000 mB Superfluid Helium.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Artificial Intelligence.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Aleph-Null Shard, Aleph-One, Anomaly Catalogue, Cognitive Singularity, Computronium Ingot, Contagion Network Map, Dimensional Residue, Error-Correction Lattice and more.

A thought frozen in a lattice so that it can be copied, stored and read back. Each node holds a fragment of a pattern of neurons, and together they hold the idea whole. Holding it, I occasionally find myself remembering something I never thought.
pages.title: Thought Matrix

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Psionic Resonator, I pressed a Psionic Crystal against a Neural Lattice with Psionic Ether. The thought I was holding transferred into the lattice and stayed there, readable later by anyone who touched it.

pages.text: I must be honest in my own notebook: there is no known physics of psionics. Thought, as far as anyone knows, is electrochemistry in neurons. Yet the resonator works. I record; I do not yet explain.

pages.text: Feynman, 1959: 'There's plenty of room at the bottom.' Von Neumann had already shown a machine could carry its own blueprint and copy itself. This foundry is both ideas in one box. I watch it the way one watches a sleeping dog.

One cell of claytronics: a tiny module that can join with others, move across their surfaces and form any shape. Millions of catoms together can become anything at all. A single one is a smooth bead that rolls toward its neighbours whenever it can.
pages.title: Claytronic Catom

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Nanite Assembler, I packed programmable matter into a Superposition Crystal shell. The result could hold many shapes at once, and it could combine with others into any form I asked for.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Nanite Assembler$() from 6 Programmable Matter, 12 Superposition Crystal, 6 Antimatter Pellet, 24 Xenogenome Sample, 8,000 mB Nanite Slurry, 8,000 mB Tachyon Flux.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Molecular Nanotechnology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Reality Anchor, Von Neumann Probe.

A suspension of microscopic machines in water. The slurry moves on its own, shifting patterns across its surface as the nanites communicate. It feels faintly gritty and warm. Left in a bucket overnight, it rearranges itself into neat geometric ridges by morning.
pages.title: Nanite Slurry

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Condensing a Nanite Swarm with water, the nanites spread through the liquid and began working together. The slurry could be poured into moulds and would build whatever they were told.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Bose-Einstein Condenser$() from 4 Nanite Swarm, 4 Coherent Wiring Harness, 16,000 mB Water.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Molecular Nanotechnology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Claytronic Catom, Cognitive Singularity, Contained Anomaly Specimen, Inertia Damper, Programmable Matter, Von Neumann Probe.

A billion machines the size of viruses, each one able to grab, move and bond individual atoms. Together they can build or unbuild almost anything, and they are hungry for raw material. The swarm looks like a grey cloud that shimmers at the edges.
pages.title: Nanite Swarm

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Nanite Assembler, I programmed a Maxwell's Demon Chip to sort atoms, then gave it quantum dots for sight and neutronium for hands. It began copying itself. Wild swarms drop the same, which worried me.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Nanite Assembler$() from 12 Quantum Dot, 6 Neutronium Plate, 6 Maxwell's Demon Chip, 12 Chiral Crystal, 8,000 mB Superfluid Helium, 8,000 mB Supercritical Solvent.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Nanite Swarm.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Molecular Nanotechnology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Contained Anomaly Specimen, Graphene Sheet, Nanite Slurry, Programmable Matter, Quine Replicator, Xenobot Swarm.

Matter that changes its own shape and properties on command. Nanites rearrange its structure, metamaterial tunes its response, and a qubit holds the instructions. Squeeze it and it becomes harder; ask it politely and it becomes a key.
pages.title: Programmable Matter

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)A Nanite Swarm in Nanite Slurry, with a Metamaterial Sheet and a Qubit in the Nanite Assembler, settled into a single shapeable mass. I told it to be a cup and it became one, then a sphere, then a spanner.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Nanite Assembler$() from 24 Nanite Swarm, 6 Metamaterial Sheet, 6 Qubit, 6 Rational Field, 16,000 mB Nanite Slurry, 8,000 mB Superfluid Helium.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Molecular Nanotechnology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Claytronic Catom.

Life's first molecules polymerise (Arrhenius, Eₐ = 60 kJ/mol) while water hydrolyses them (80 kJ/mol). Copying is imperfect: Eigen's error threshold says a genome of length L survives only if L < ln σ / µ. Sparks drive chemistry but also mutate.
$(thing)Set$(): Reactor temperature, Monomer concentration, Spark & UV flux.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Temperature swings: the error rate varies by ±10%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): Error catastrophe: the genome cannot persist; The crucible cannot be held colder than its coolant.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Synthesis rate follows the yield and the energy supply.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Polymerisation rate: k = A·e^(−Eₐ/RT)$(br)Hydrolysis rate: k_h = A_h·e^(−E_h/RT)$(br)Polymer yield: Y = k_p c/(k_p c + k_h)$(br)Copy error µ: µ$(br)Error threshold: L_max = ln σ / µ

Proton-antiproton annihilation turns mass entirely into pions: about half the energy in charged pions (p ≈ 0.35 GeV/c), a third in gamma rays, the rest in neutrinos. A magnetic nozzle can catch the charged pions if their gyroradius p/(0.3B) fits the 3 m chamber; the gammas must be stopped by shielding.
$(thing)Set$(): Nozzle field, Antimatter feed, Gamma shield.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Annihilation-point jitter: capture varies by ±5%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): Gamma flux through the shield is melting the structure; Interlock: magnetic nozzle not superconducting (too warm); Field above the critical field: the magnetic nozzle quench.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Generator output follows the captured power.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Annihilation power: P = 2ṁc²$(br)Pion gyroradius: r_g = p/(0.3B)$(br)Capture fraction: f = 1 − r_g/R$(br)Electric power: P_e = ½P·f$(br)Gamma power: P_γ = ⅓P$(br)Escaping gammas: P_γ·e^(−x/20 cm)$(br)Critical field: B_c(T) = B_c2(0)·(1 − (T/T_c)²)

A specimen copies itself at a rate β; the ward clears it at its natural rate γ = 0.4 per day plus the quarantine field's own rate q. Each anomalous unit then makes R = β/(γ + q) more before it is cleared. Below 1 the specimen is contained and can be studied; the faster it grows the more there is to study - but at R above 1 it spreads through the containment. Clamp the field too hard and the specimen goes dormant and there is nothing to learn.
$(thing)Set$(): Growth rate β, Quarantine rate q.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): The specimen's growth rate wanders by ±10%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): R above 1: the anomaly is spreading through the containment; The quarantine is so strong the specimen has gone dormant: nothing to study; The quarantine field is overheating the ward.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): A faster-growing specimen held just below R = 1 gives the most to study.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Effective growth rate: β_eff = β·(1 + 0.1·d)$(br)Reproduction number R: R = β/(γ + q)$(br)Observable activity: A = β·R

The anomaly is dosed in n fractions of D. Each fraction kills a fraction exp(−αD − βD²) of its 10⁹ clonogenic cells (α = 0.3 Gy⁻¹, β = 0.03 Gy⁻²); it is resolved when none survives, with probability TCP = exp(−N₀·e^{−n(αD + βD²)}). The normal tissue around it repairs between fractions, but its damage grows as BED = nD(1 + D/3): small fractions spare it, large ones do not.
$(thing)Set$(): Dose per fraction D, Fractions n.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): The anomaly's sensitivity α wanders by ±5%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): The anomaly survives: too many of its clonogens are left; The dose is destroying the normal tissue around the anomaly; The resolution fields are overheating.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): The surer the resolution, the faster the work goes.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Sensitivity α: α = 0.3·(1 + 0.05·d)$(br)Log cell kill: ln(1/S) = n(αD + βD²)$(br)Resolution probability TCP: TCP = exp(−N₀·e^{−n(αD + βD²)})$(br)Normal-tissue BED: BED₃ = nD(1 + D/3)

A breach is a bubble of different vacuum (Coleman-De Luccia). A wall of tension σ around a region whose energy is lower by Δε has critical radius R = 3σ/Δε, and the nucleation rate goes as exp(−B), B = 27π²σ⁴/(2Δε³). Too fast, and the bubble swallows everything.
$(thing)Set$(): Wall tension σ, Energy difference Δε, Barrier field.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Vacuum energy noise: Δε·(1 ± 0.2%·d).

$(thing)Limits$(): Bubbles everywhere: the breach spreads beyond the chamber; Barrier not shaped: the wall cannot form; Interlock: barrier-shaping coils not superconducting (too warm); Field above the critical field: the barrier-shaping coils quench.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): The breach runs at a fixed pace.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Critical radius: R_c = 3σ/Δε$(br)Bounce action B: B = 27π²σ⁴/(2Δε³)$(br)Bubbles per second: N = Δε·e^(−B)·V·t$(br)Critical field: B_c(T) = B_c2(0)·(1 − (T/T_c)²)

Take one mouth of a wormhole on a fast round trip: it ages less (twin paradox). Once its time lag exceeds the light-travel time between the mouths, the pair is a time machine - a closed timelike curve. Near that threshold, vacuum fluctuations pile up (Hawking's chronology protection).
$(thing)Set$(): Mouth speed, Trip duration, Mouth separation, Steering field.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Mouth trajectory error: the trip speed is v·(1 ± 0.01%·d).

$(thing)Limits$(): No closed timelike curve yet: the lag is shorter than the light time; Chronology protection: vacuum polarisation diverges at the Cauchy horizon; Close to the chronology horizon: the structure strains; Steering field too weak for that turnaround; Interlock: mouth-steering coils not superconducting (too warm); Field above the critical field: the mouth-steering coils quench.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Loops run at a fixed pace.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Lorentz factor: γ = 1/√(1 − v²)$(br)Time lag: Δt = T(1 − 1/γ)$(br)Light time: t_L = L/c$(br)Loop length: Δt − L/c$(br)Lag / light time: Δt/(L/c)$(br)Turnaround acceleration: a = γvc/(T/2)$(br)Critical field: B_c(T) = B_c2(0)·(1 − (T/T_c)²)

The $(item)Chronal Accelerator$() wraps a cube of space in a closed timelike shell and lets time inside run faster - x2 up to x256. Every machine, furnace, block entity of any mod, and every growing thing (crops, saplings, ores of the Bulk) inside the cube runs that many times faster.
$(thing)Right-click$() to change the speed, $(thing)sneak-right-click$() to change the size of the field (3x3x3 up to 9x9x9). A redstone signal stops it. It glows while it is working.

It is ruinous to run. Every extra tick it gives one block entity costs $(thing)65,536 FE$(); every extra random tick to a growing block 16,384 FE; and every eight extra ticks one mB of $(item)Chronon Gas$(). A single machine at x256 eats about 16.7 million FE and 32 mB of gas per tick. When it runs short it simply does nothing that tick.

Feed it energy and Chronon Gas from any side. Pack makers: the costs, the top speed and the largest field are in the common config; the block tag theoreticalsciences:not_accelerated lists blocks it will never touch. It never accelerates another accelerator, and the $(item)Chronal Field Projector$() (which only sets the rate of time for this mod's recipes) is a different thing.

Shannon's source coding theorem: a source of entropy H bits per symbol can be compressed to any rate R above H - and to none below. At finite block length n, the error falls as exp(−n(R−H)²/2V). Every concept has its own entropy.
$(thing)Set$(): Code rate R, Block length n, Store field.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Source drift: the concept's entropy fluctuates by ±1%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): Rate below the entropy: information is destroyed; Store field too weak for that rate; Interlock: holographic-store coils not superconducting (too warm); Field above the critical field: the holographic-store coils quench.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Shorter blocks compress faster.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Entropy H: H = −q log q − (1−q) log(1−q)$(br)Dispersion V: V = q(1−q)·log²((1−q)/q)$(br)Rate margin R − H: R − H$(br)Error probability: P_e ≈ exp(−n(R−H)²/2V)$(br)Compression ratio: 1/R$(br)Critical field: B_c(T) = B_c2(0)·(1 − (T/T_c)²)

Every multiblock has a $(thing)coolant loop$(): pipe a coolant into it (or click its tank with a filled container). The coolant holds the cold mass near its own temperature; whatever heat the machine makes raises it by heat/κ.

Coolants: Water and Ionic Liquid (300 K), Superfluid Helium and Liquid Antihelium (2 K), Neutrino Flux (10 K), Metallic Hydrogen and Antihydrogen (20 K), Dark Matter and Liquid Spacetime (3 K), and a Bose-Einstein Condensate at 10 mK that carries almost no heat.

Superfluid Helium comes back out as $(fluid)Warm Helium$() in the spent tank: send it to a Condensing Chamber and back. If the spent tank fills, the loop stops - and without coolant a machine only sheds heat slowly to the air.

Coils are superconductors with a critical temperature and field: Nb-Ti (tier 1) 9.2 K and 14.5 T, Nb₃Sn 18.3 K and 30 T, REBCO 92 K and 120 T, neutronium hydride 290 K and 400 T, transfinite lattice 4000 K. The usable field falls as B_c2(0)·(1 − (T/T_c)²): the colder, the stronger.

Run a magnet above its critical field and it $(thing)quenches$(). Above 95% of T_c the interlock will not even let it start. So heat is not just a cost: every kilowatt raises the temperature, and with it lowers the field you can use.

Two plates a hair apart exclude vacuum modes from the gap: a Casimir pressure P = π²ħc/(240a⁴) pushes them together, and the vacuum between them holds negative energy. At about 30 µm that energy density equals the dark energy of the universe.
$(thing)Set$(): Plate gap a, Plate area, Cycle rate, Plate stiffness.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Plate parallelism error: the effective gap is a·(1 + 0.5%·d).

$(thing)Limits$(): Casimir pull-in: the plates snap together; Thermal photons swamp the vacuum signal: cool the plates; The plate stack is overheating.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Plate area swept per second.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Effective gap: a_eff$(br)Casimir pressure: P = π²ħc/(240a⁴)$(br)Vacuum energy density: |u| = π²ħc/(720a⁴)$(br)Energy density / ρ_Λ: log₁₀(|u|/ρ_Λ)$(br)Force gradient: dF/da = 4PA/a$(br)Thermal wavelength: λ_T = ħc/kT$(br)Extracted power: P = |u|·A·a·f

Dark matter streams through at ~230 km/s. A WIMP of mass m_χ hitting a nucleus of mass m_N can give it at most 2µ²v²/m_N of recoil - so match the target to the WIMP. Bolometers resolve ΔE ∝ T^(5/2): light dark matter needs millikelvin.
$(thing)Set$(): Target mass number, Recoil threshold, Detector mass, Shield field.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Neutron background varies by ±30%·d.

Every multiblock is a real machine now. Its $(thing)Operation$() console (right of its screen) has three pages.$(br2)$(thing)Controls$(): the parameters you set - fields, voltages, currents, gaps. Click a value to type it, scroll to step it.

$(thing)Readout$(): everything that follows from your settings, worked out with real equations. Hover any line for its formula. Below them, the $(thing)limits$() the machine must respect and the $(thing)recipe window$() it must be run inside.
Each recipe states a window - a beam energy, a plasma temperature, a density, a significance. JEI shows it under the recipe. If the readout is outside it, the machine waits: $(thing)Out of Window$().

Limits come in four kinds. Some simply stop the machine. Some make it $(thing)strain$() - containment wears four times as fast. Some $(thing)damage$() it every second. And some $(thing)quench$(): the stored energy dumps as heat in an instant, the containment takes a hit, and the machine needs eight seconds to recover. Enough of those and containment fails.

The $(thing)disturbance$() d (Plant page) is what the machine fights: field errors, drifting phases, impurities, outgassing. It moves while the machine runs, and every model says what it does. A Field Calibrator trims it back to zero; an Autonomous Calibrator damps it.

Structures may cross chunk borders freely. Away from home, a $(thing)chunk loader$() keeps a machine running: load every chunk the structure touches. If only some are loaded, the controller keeps the state it last saw (formed, its ports) and waits - it never reaches into an unloaded chunk.

Third dive. The Quantum Foam has a floor and a ceiling I cannot pass. Below lies $(item)Schrödinger's Limit$(), where every possibility is still undecided.

Above lies $(item)Relativity Breakdown$(), where spacetime stops being smooth - the scale where general relativity and quantum mechanics both fail at once.$(br2)Both are liquids that will not flow and cannot be crossed. Fill a cell from either and it is still there - they regenerate at once.

Schrödinger's Limit becomes the concepts of quantum mechanics in the $(item)Analytic Continuator$(): $(item)Wavefunctions$(), the $(item)Hamiltonian$(), $(item)Eigenstates$(), the $(item)Path Integral$().

Relativity Breakdown becomes $(item)Geodesics$(), $(item)Christoffel Symbols$() and the $(item)Stress-Energy Tensor$() in the $(item)Chrono Loom$(). The two great theories of the last century, bottled separately. Someday I must make them agree.

pages.text: Day 37. In real metamaterials, structure smaller than a wavelength can give a negative refractive index: light bends to the wrong side of the normal. That is the trick behind laboratory invisibility cloaks. This machine weaves such lattices - and, it seems, for gravity as well.

Thousands of atoms behaving as one. Chilled to within a whisper of absolute zero, they share a single wavefunction and slide as a single wave, rippling with interference fringes. It looks like a faint mist that refuses to scatter.
pages.title: Bose-Einstein Condensate

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Seeding superfluid helium with quantum dots in the Bose-Einstein Condenser, I watched the atoms' wave packets swell until they overlapped and fused into one. Matter forgot it was many particles.

A closed-cycle superfluid refrigerator. It pumps heat out of a superconducting magnet and keeps it below its critical temperature, without which the superconductor would stop superconducting. It frosts over in seconds and makes a soft, steady sigh.
pages.title: Cryocooler Unit

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)My magnets kept quenching. In the Bose-Einstein Condenser, I built a cycle where superfluid helium flowed between Casimir Plates, carrying heat out without friction. I later found a few in derelict stations.
