pages.title: Brane Strider

pages.text: A humming lattice that keeps my wavefunction from decohering into a thousand slightly different versions of me. Normally the environment measures a body constantly; this device shelters me from enough of that scrutiny to stay one thing. It feels heavier when I think about it too hard.
pages.title: Coherence Stabiliser

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Quantum Foam I watched my own outline blur into overlapping drafts. I braided an entangled photon pair through a quantum field lattice and a spin foam lattice on a chronosteel frame, so that it carries the decoherence away from me instead.
$(thing)Made$(): Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$() from 36 Quantum Field Lattice, 36 Entangled Photon Pair, 9 Spin Foam Lattice.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Quantum Gravity.

A circuit board laid across a Calabi-Yau manifold, its traces running through six compact dimensions. It holds circuits far larger than its surface, folded through hidden space. Turning it over, I can see the traces continue on the back, and into somewhere else.
pages.title: Cosmic Circuit Board

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Tesseract Assembler, I wrapped a Metamaterial Substrate around a Calabi-Yau Manifold with a Cosmic String Segment, an Attoscale Inductor and Exotic Solder. The traces followed every dimension.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Tesseract Assembler$() from 48 Metamaterial Substrate, 12 Calabi-Yau Manifold, 12 Cosmic String Segment, 96 Attoscale Inductor, 24 Chronoplastic Gasket, 73,728 mB Exotic Solder, 32,000 mB Synaptic Fluid and more.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Multiverse.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Processor, Ontological Processor, Transfinite Processor, Unified Notes II.

A die holding a galaxy-scale computation folded into a square I can pinch between two fingers. Its traces stretch across light-years inside the fold. In the dark it glimmers faintly, like a patch of night sky.
pages.title: Cosmic Die

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Cutting a Cosmic Logic Wafer in the Planck-Scale Cutter, I worried the light-year traces would unfold. Superfluid helium held them still while the cutter separated each die.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Planck-Scale Cutter$() from 4 Cosmic Logic Wafer, 4 Coherent Wiring Harness, 1,600 mB Superfluid Helium.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Multiverse.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Processor, Unified Notes III.

A loop of cosmic string that bends light into perfect focus. The missing wedge of space around the string acts as an ideal lens, with no aberration at all. It is a thin circle of light that hums faintly and never needs replacing.
pages.title: Cosmic String Lens

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)On the String Resonance Loom, I bent a Cosmic String Segment around a Tesseract Lens with a Graviton Crystal. The loop's conical space focused light more perfectly than any glass could.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)String Resonance Loom$() from 24 Cosmic String Segment, 12 Tesseract Lens, 12 Graviton Crystal, 12 Spacetime Catalyst, 128,000 mB Exotic Matter.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Multiverse.

Etched with a lens made from a cosmic string, each trace on this wafer is a light-year long, folded into itself. It holds circuits on a galactic scale in a disc I can carry. The surface is dark, scattered with faint points like distant stars.
pages.title: Cosmic Logic Wafer

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Quantum Lithographer I engraved a Hyperdimensional Wafer through Quantum-Dot Photoresist, focused by a loop of cosmic string. The string folded each trace across a light-year of space.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Quantum Lithographer$() from 4 Hyperdimensional Wafer, 4 Coherent Wiring Harness, 1,600 mB Quantum-Dot Photoresist.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Multiverse.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Die, Unified Notes I, Warm Helium.

The fifth tier of processor: a computer the size of a galaxy, folded into a chip. Its traces stretch across light-years through the fold, and its computation runs at a cosmic scale. It is dark and starry, and warm with constant thought.
pages.title: Cosmic Processor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)On the Femtoscale Assembly Line, I placed a Cosmic Die on a Cosmic Circuit Board with a Hyperdimensional Processor and attoscale parts. The resulting chip computed the orbits of a galaxy in seconds.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() from 8 Cosmic Circuit Board, 32 Cosmic Die, 16 Hyperdimensional Processor, 128 Attoscale Capacitor, 128 Attoscale Transistor, 36,864 mB Causal Solder, 128,000 mB Superfluid Helium and more.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Multiverse.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Pedestal, Autonomous Calibrator, Cantor Diagonalizer, Conceptual Singularity Compressor, Convergence Engine, Cosmic Flux Coupler, Dimensional Residue, Entangled Transceiver and more.

A casing built to contain the birth of a universe. Spin foam lattice, multiverse shard and cosmic neutronium are folded over a hyperlattice frame, around rift frame casing. It is unpleasantly heavy and quietly warm.
pages.title: Cosmogenic Casing

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The Universe Forge needed a shell strong enough for a Big Bang. Spin foam is the fabric of quantum spacetime, a multiverse shard is the boundary between universes, and cosmic neutronium held them both.

$(thing)Made$(): Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$() from 36 Multiverse Shard, 36 Spin Foam Lattice, 9 Rift Frame Casing.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Quantum Gravity.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Inflation Chamber, Reality Lattice Casing, Universe Forge.

A surface on which open strings can end, with its own dynamics and its own charge. Our universe could be a three-dimensional D-brane floating in higher dimensions. The sheet ripples like silk, and strings seem to cling to it.
pages.title: D-Brane Sheet

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Stretching quantum strings across metamaterial with brane tension fiber in the Compactification Lathe, I noticed their ends stuck to the sheet. Exotic matter held it rigid enough to keep.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Compactification Lathe$() from 48 Quantum String, 24 Brane Tension Fiber, 12 Metamaterial Sheet, 12 Pulsar Timing Crystal, 64,000 mB Exotic Matter.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compactification.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Singularity, M-Brane.

Space in a higher-energy state than it should be, metastable and fragile. Contained, it looks like perfectly clear liquid, but the energy it stores is the energy of an entire universe waiting to tunnel down. I handle it gently.
pages.title: False Vacuum

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Running a False Vacuum Membrane through the Bose-Einstein Condenser with superfluid helium, I found the condensate stabilised the metastable state long enough to bottle it. Coleman would not approve.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Bose-Einstein Condenser$() from 4 False Vacuum Membrane, 4 Coherent Wiring Harness, 8,000 mB Superfluid Helium.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Multiverse.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Exotic Matter Singularity, False Vacuum Membrane, Foam Substrate, Inflaton Condensate, Metastable Vacuum Lattice, Pocket Universe, Relativity Breakdown and more.

Seven curled dimensions with a special holonomy whose symmetry group, G2, is the automorphism group of the octonions. M-theory on such a space gives a four-dimensional world with realistic physics. The manifold is tightly folded and seems to have no inside or outside.
pages.title: G₂ Manifold

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Combining a Calabi-Yau with an extra moduli direction and the octonions' symmetry, the Compactification Lathe produced a seven-dimensional manifold with G2 holonomy, held open by exotic matter.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Compactification Lathe$() from 12 Calabi-Yau Manifold, 48 Moduli Crystal, 12 Octonion Crystal, 12 Grand Unified Core, 128,000 mB Exotic Matter.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compactification.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Dimensional Singularity, E8 Lattice, M-Brane, M-Theory Core.

A device that keeps its bearer's worldline intact inside a black or white hole. Without it, tidal forces and causal chaos are lethal within seconds. It is heavy and cool and hums faintly, like a gyroscope.
pages.title: Geodesic Anchor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Inside a black hole I nearly lost my worldline. Combining a Kerr metric shard, graviton crystal and chronon capacitor in a hyperlattice frame on the Extreme Assembly Table, I built an anchor to keep it.
$(thing)Made$(): Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$() from 36 Neutronium Plate, 18 Graviton Crystal, 18 Kerr Metric Shard, 9 Chronon Capacitor.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compactification.

At sufficiently high energy, the electromagnetic, weak and strong couplings run together and meet. Grand unified theories predict magnetic monopoles and proton decay as a consequence. The core is bright and calm, three forces resting in a single symmetry.
pages.title: Grand Unified Core

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Running the Standard Model's couplings upward with superpartners included, I saw them converge. In the Tesseract Assembler, a monopole and a quantum string held the high-energy state long enough to crystallise it.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Tesseract Assembler$() from 24 Standard Model Matrix, 48 Superpartner Shard, 48 Magnetic Monopole, 48 Quantum String, 24 Chronoplastic Gasket, 512,000 mB Quark-Gluon Plasma, 256,000 mB Exotic Matter and more.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Grand Unification.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Standard Model Singularity, Theory of Everything, Transcendent Metal Ingot, Transcendent Plasma.

Gravitons are the hypothetical quanta of gravity, and this crystal holds them frozen in a lattice. It feels heavier than it is: the stored gravitons pull on my hand as well as on the floor. Near it, falling dust curves slightly toward the crystal before reaching the ground.
pages.title: Graviton Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I cooled Virtual Gravitons from the quantum foam in Superfluid Helium inside the Graviton Condenser until they could not escape. Graviton Wisps carry them naturally, and I found more in vaults, monoliths and derelict stations.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Graviton Condenser$() from 12 Micro Singularity, 12 Quantum String, 12 Computronium Singularity, 128,000 mB Hawking Radiation.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Graviton Wisp.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Anomaly Vault, Bulk Monolith, Derelict Station chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compactification.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Brane Tether, Bulk Crystal, Bulk Stone, Compactification Lathe, Cosmic Processor, Cosmic String Lens, False Vacuum, Geodesic Anchor and more.

A web of straps and plates that takes the pull of a crushing field and spreads it through every bone at once, so no single joint bears it. Tidal forces kill by difference, not by strength; the harness erases the difference. Wearing it feels like being hugged by a planet.
pages.title: Graviton Harness

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)A walk through a high-gravity field nearly broke both my ankles. I laid graviton crystals across neutronium plating and added an inertia damper to smooth the gradients, so that the field pulls on all of me equally and none of me in particular.
$(thing)Made$(): Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$() from 36 Neutronium Plate, 27 Graviton Crystal, 9 Inertia Damper.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compactification.
$(thing)Graviton Wisp$(). Lives in: Graviton Reef, The Bulk.$(br)Drops: Graviton Wisp Core, Graviton Crystal, Void Lattice Shard.
pages.title: Graviton Wisp

pages.text: All that is left of a universe that has reached maximum entropy: no stars, no gradients, nothing to drive any process at all. It is cold, perfectly even and perfectly still, a uniform grey with no texture to catch the light. Holding it feels like holding silence.
pages.title: Heat Death Remnant

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I let a Pocket Universe in the Universe Forge run to its end. Trillions of years compressed into a few minutes, and the bubble came out like this: inert, even, and oddly peaceful. Its stillness is what makes new universes possible.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Entropy Horizon$() from 64 Heat Death Ember, 16 De Sitter Horizon Shard, 25,600 mB Dark Era Haze.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Cosmogenesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Boltzmann Brain, Inflaton Field, Universe Seed.
A scalar field held at the top of its potential, rolling so slowly that space doubles many times before it moves.
pages.title: Inflaton Condensate

pages.text: $(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Inflation Chamber$() from 16 Graviton Crystal, 16 Dark Matter Lens, 64,000 mB Inflaton Field, 25,600 mB False Vacuum.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Cosmic Inflation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): No-Boundary Seed, Pocket Universe, Reheating Plasma, Universe Seed.

A two-dimensional membrane from M-theory, the eleven-dimensional framework in which strings are the edges of membranes. A brane like this could host an entire universe on its surface, with gravity alone leaking into the Bulk. It is a sheet of light that ripples when I breathe on it.
pages.title: M-Brane

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I wove a D-Brane Sheet with a G2 Manifold and a String Coupling Crystal on the String Resonance Loom, turning the coupling up until the strings fused into a membrane. Eleven dimensions, counted twice to make sure.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)String Resonance Loom$() from 24 D-Brane Sheet, 12 G₂ Manifold, 12 String Coupling Crystal, 12 Room-Temperature Superconductor, 128,000 mB Exotic Matter.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): M-Theory.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Dimensional Singularity, Exotic Matter Crystal, Inflaton Field, M-Theory Core, Multiverse Shard, Penteract Display, Theoretical Notes II and more.

Five superstring theories turned out to be limits of one eleven-dimensional theory, whose fundamental objects include membranes as well as strings. Witten called it M-theory, and nobody knows what the M stands for. The core vibrates in more directions than seem possible.
pages.title: M-Theory Core

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Wrapping an M-brane on a G2 manifold and a compactified circle in the Compactification Lathe, I found all five string theories as limits of one. Exotic matter kept the eleventh dimension open.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Compactification Lathe$() from 24 M-Brane, 12 G₂ Manifold, 48 Compactified Circle, 12 Rift Anchor, 256,000 mB Exotic Matter.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): M-Theory.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Singularity, Theory of Everything.
The Higgs potential mapped out to the Planck scale: the valley we live in is not the deepest one. Held in a lattice of Higgs field capacitors.
pages.title: Metastable Vacuum Lattice

pages.text: $(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Higgs Field Modulator$() from 16 Higgs Field Capacitor, 8 Magnetic Monopole, 16,000 mB False Vacuum.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Vacuum Stability.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): No-Boundary Seed, Topological Defect Core, True Vacuum Seed.
A closed universe tunnelled from nothing: round, without an edge, and without a first moment of time.
pages.title: No-Boundary Seed

pages.text: $(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Inflation Chamber$() from 16 Spin Foam Lattice, 32 Inflaton Condensate, 16 Metastable Vacuum Lattice, 25,600 mB Reheating Plasma.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Creation from Nothing.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Universe Seed.

A one-dimensional vibrating string, the fundamental object of string theory. Its mode of vibration decides what it is: one note an electron, another a photon, another a graviton. In the hand it is a thread of light that hums, changing its tune slightly with my pulse.
pages.title: Quantum String

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The String Resonance Loom stretched a Cosmic String Segment down to the Planck scale, tuned it with a Tachyon Crystal and held it in a Superposition Crystal. When it began to vibrate in discrete modes, I knew it was a string.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)String Resonance Loom$() from 12 Cosmic String Segment, 12 Tachyon Crystal, 12 Superposition Crystal, 12 Bekenstein Crystal, 32,000 mB Exotic Matter.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Calabi Yau Knot chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): String Theory.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Brane Tension Fiber, Compactified Circle, D-Brane Sheet, Dimensional Residue, Dimensional Stabiliser Matrix, Grand Unified Core, Graviton Crystal, String Coupling Crystal.
$(fluid)Reheating Plasma$().
pages.title: Reheating Plasma

pages.text: $(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Inflation Chamber$() from 16 Inflaton Condensate, 12,800 mB Quark-Gluon Plasma.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Reheating.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Baryogenesis Seed, Baryon Asymmetry Crystal, No-Boundary Seed, Pocket Universe, Primordial Nucleosynthesis Ash, Universe Seed.

$(thing)Conformal Cyclic Cosmology$()$(br2)At the end of time only massless things remain, and massless things cannot tell an infinite distance from a finite one. Rescale the dead universe and its infinite future becomes the Big Bang of the next aeon.
pages.title: Conformal Cyclic Cosmology

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 280$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Creation from Nothing, Heat Death, Cosmogenesis.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 De Sitter Horizon Shard.

$(thing)Leptogenesis$()$(br2)Matter and antimatter should have annihilated perfectly. They did not: heavy neutrinos decayed out of equilibrium, unequally to leptons and antileptons, and sphalerons turned the excess into baryons - one in a billion. Unlocks the Baryon Asymmetry Crystal.
pages.title: Leptogenesis

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 190$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Reheating, Neutrino Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 8 Sterile Neutrino.
$(thing)M-Theory$()$(br2)Strings are the edges of membranes in eleven dimensions.
pages.title: M-Theory

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 120$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): String Theory, Brane Cosmology, Compactification.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Quantum String.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Find the 11-dimensional Planck length of M-theory from the string coupling gs and string length ls.

$(thing)Creation from Nothing$()$(br2)Before inflation, before time: a closed universe can tunnel into existence from no space at all, or begin without a boundary, its time becoming space near the start like the South Pole of a sphere. Quantum cosmology writes the wave function of the whole universe.
pages.title: Creation from Nothing

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 220$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Reheating, Vacuum Stability, Quantum Gravity.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Spin Foam Lattice.

$(thing)Reheating$()$(br2)Inflation leaves space empty and cold. When the inflaton reaches the bottom of its potential it oscillates and decays, and its energy becomes a hot plasma of every particle there is: the hot Big Bang begins here. Unlocks Reheating Plasma.
pages.title: Reheating

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 170$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Cosmic Inflation, High-Energy Particle Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Strange Matter Pellet.

$(thing)Vacuum Stability$()$(br2)What could stop a universe from starting at all? A vacuum energy a little larger and it would fly apart before stars formed; a Higgs coupling a little smaller and the vacuum would be unstable. Ours sits, by measurement, at the edge: metastable. Unlocks the Metastable Vacuum Lattice.
pages.title: Vacuum Stability

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 180$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Cosmic Inflation, The Standard Model.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Higgs Field Capacitor.

A clamp for tears between universes. Graviton crystals pin the edges of the rift, void lattice keeps the Bulk from closing in, and exotic matter props the gap open just long enough to reach through. It vibrates faintly, as if something on the other side were tugging back.
pages.title: Rift Anchor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Every rift I opened closed before I could use it. In the Graviton Condenser I bound a Graviton Crystal to a Void Lattice Shard with Exotic Matter, and the next rift stayed open long enough for me to put my hand through.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Graviton Condenser$() from 24 Graviton Crystal, 12 Void Lattice Shard, 12 Hyperdimensional Boule, 128,000 mB Exotic Matter.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Multiverse.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Exotic Matter Crystal, Inflaton Field, Multiverse Rift Stabilizer, Multiverse Shard, Void Lattice Shard.

A casing reinforced against tearing open: void lattice, graviton crystal and chronosteel over a hyperframe. It is built to sit at the edge of a rift between universes, and it feels faintly cold on one side.
pages.title: Rift Frame Casing

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Stabilising a multiverse rift tore through every casing I tried. I layered a void lattice shard, which is rigid even with nothing in it, over a hyperframe with graviton crystal to hold the geometry. It held.

$(thing)Made$(): Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$() from 36 Void Lattice Shard, 36 Graviton Crystal, 9 Hyperframe Casing.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compactification.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmogenic Casing, Multiverse Rift Stabilizer.

A pylon that pins a patch of spacetime in place, built around a spacetime anchor core and a chronosteel coil. The ground around it feels unusually solid, as if gravity had made its mind up. Compasses near it point steady.
pages.title: Spacetime Anchor Pylon

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Large machines warped the ground they stood on. I built a pylon around an anchor core with a chronosteel coil and hyperframe casing, and the warping stopped at its edge.
$(thing)Made$(): Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$() from 36 Spacetime Anchor Core, 36 Hyperframe Casing, 9 Chronosteel Coil Block.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Quantum Gravity.

A lattice of spin networks evolving in time, the loop quantum gravity picture of spacetime as discrete quanta of area and volume. It looks like a soap foam frozen in place, but each bubble is a quantum of space itself. Pressing it does not compress it; space does not come in smaller units.

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I fed Graviton Crystals through the Graviton Condenser together with a qubit to track the states and a condensate to hold them coherent. Spacetime started showing up in discrete chunks, which loop gravity had promised.

Two branches of physics are about time itself: $(thing)Origin$(), how a universe begins, and $(thing)Finality$(), how it ends. Origin starts with $(thing)The Hot Big Bang$(): run the expansion backwards and everything was once hotter and denser than the core of a star.

The $(thing)Friedmann equation$() says how fast space expands: H² = 8πGρ/3 − kc²/a² + Λc²/3. Matter and radiation slow it, curvature bends it, and the vacuum energy Λ - dark energy - takes over in the end. Exactly flat space has the critical density, about five protons per cubic metre.

$(li)$(thing)Primordial Nucleosynthesis$(): for three minutes the universe fused hydrogen into helium. $(item)Primordial Nucleosynthesis Ash$() comes from quark-gluon plasma (or reheating plasma) in the $(item)Nucleosynthesis Chamber$().$(li)$(thing)Cosmic Inflation$() and $(thing)Reheating$(): see the next chapter.$(li)$(thing)Leptogenesis$(), $(thing)Vacuum Stability$(), $(thing)Creation from Nothing$() and $(thing)Conformal Cyclic Cosmology$() come after.

Where Finality ends, Origin begins. Roger Penrose noticed that at the end of a heat death only massless particles remain - and light has no clock: it cannot tell an infinitely large, cold universe from a tiny, hot one. Rescale the dead universe's infinite future and it is the Big Bang of the next $(thing)aeon$().

In the $(item)Inflation Chamber$(): $(item)Heat Death Embers$(), a $(item)De Sitter Horizon Shard$() and $(fluid)Dark Era Haze$() make an $(item)Aeon Boundary Shard$(); the Shard with a $(item)No-Boundary Seed$() and inflaton condensate makes two $(item)Universe Seeds$(). A $(item)Bounce Core$() from a Big Crunch makes one too.

Origin also feeds what came before it: the $(item)Universe Forge$() can make a $(item)Pocket Universe$() from first principles - a seed, a true-vacuum bubble, the asymmetry, the ash and the plasma - and the Eye of the Horizon's and the Omnilex's universes now want Primordial Ash and a No-Boundary Seed.

The Big Bang alone cannot explain why opposite sides of the sky have the same temperature to one part in 100,000: they were never in contact. $(thing)Inflation$() does: before the hot Big Bang, a scalar field - the inflaton - sat high on its potential and made space grow exponentially, sixty e-folds in 10⁻³² s.

Build the $(item)Inflation Chamber$(). It condenses the $(fluid)Inflaton Field$() and $(fluid)False Vacuum$() into $(item)Inflaton Condensate$(). In its Operation console keep the slow-roll ε = 2/φ² below 1 and N = (φ₀² − 2)/4 above 50 - but start the field too high and inflation turns $(thing)eternal$(): quantum jumps outrun the roll, and the bubble never ends (in our universe, other bubbles still may).

$(thing)Reheating$(): at the bottom of its potential the inflaton oscillates and decays. The chamber turns Condensate and a little quark-gluon plasma into $(fluid)Reheating Plasma$() - every particle there is, at 10⁹ GeV and more. That plasma is the raw stuff of every other Origin material.

Reheating makes matter and antimatter in equal amounts, and they should have annihilated into light. For every billion photons there is one baryon left over. Andrei Sakharov's conditions say what it takes: baryon number violation, C and CP violation, and a moment out of equilibrium.

$(thing)Leptogenesis$() meets all three: heavy right-handed neutrinos decay a little more often into leptons than antileptons, and sphaleron transitions of the electroweak vacuum convert that excess into baryons. In a $(item)Quark-Gluon Collider$(), antimatter and sterile neutrinos in $(fluid)Reheating Plasma$() leave a $(item)Baryon Asymmetry Crystal$(). With the antimatter of the Antiverse, crystals become a $(item)Baryogenesis Seed$() in the $(item)Mirror Foundry$().

$(thing)Vacuum Stability$(): a universe can fail before it starts. A vacuum energy larger by a factor of a hundred and no galaxy forms; the measured one is 10¹²⁰ times smaller than quantum theory's natural guess - the $(thing)cosmological constant problem$(). And the Higgs coupling runs downwards with energy until, near 10¹⁰ GeV, a deeper vacuum opens: ours is $(thing)metastable$(). The $(item)Higgs Field Modulator$() maps it into a $(item)Metastable Vacuum Lattice$().

$(thing)Creation from Nothing$(): quantise a whole closed universe and its wave function obeys the Wheeler-DeWitt equation. Vilenkin's universe tunnels through a barrier from no space at all; Hartle and Hawking's has no boundary - near the start time turns into space, and asking what came before is like asking what is south of the South Pole.
The $(item)Inflation Chamber$() folds spin foam, inflaton condensate and a metastable vacuum into a $(item)No-Boundary Seed$().

Every journey to another dimension - by Brane Shifter, rift, wormhole, falling through the void or the hyperobject - now takes a moment: the travel animation builds up on screen for under two seconds, and only then do you jump. The loading screen of each world is its own.

Wherever you arrive, you arrive standing: never inside blocks, never in mid-air, never on top of a world's ceiling (the Quantum Foam's Relativity Breakdown, the build limit), never in a fluid or on something that burns. The ground nearby is searched for two free blocks over solid ground - open sky first, otherwise the spot nearest the height you left from.
Only when there is nowhere at all is a small platform built for you, with the room above it cleared. Laws of the place still apply: carry its attunement item.

Every strange dimension has the item that lets you survive it. Each one was made from what you brought back from the places before it - so it carries their protection too.$(br2)Carry an attunement item and every dimension whose own item comes $(l)earlier$() in this list cannot touch you at all: no debuffs, no strange gravity, no rules.
$(li)$(item)Form of the Self$(): the Platonic Realm$(li)$(item)Penning Harness$(): the Antiverse$(li)$(item)Coherence Stabiliser$(): the Quantum Foam$(li)$(item)Brane Tether$(): the Bulk

$(li)$(item)Geodesic Anchor$(): black and white holes$(li)$(item)Well-Ordering Charm$(): the Transfinite Hierarchy$(li)$(item)Primordial Charter$(): Hyperdimensional Reality$(li)$(item)Identity Kernel$(): the Transcendental$(br2)So the $(item)Primordial Charter$() shields you completely in every place before Hyperdimensional Reality, does its usual job inside Hyperdimensional Reality itself, and only the Transcendental still needs the $(item)Identity Kernel$(). In its own dimension, each item works as it always has.

Brane cosmology says our universe is a membrane adrift in a higher-dimensional $(thing)Bulk$(). The $(item)Brane Shifter$() slips me sideways into it, and back. It requires the Brane Cosmology research.

First crossing. The Bulk is an endless void of floating islands under the shadow of a vast hypercube - a four-dimensional cube, of which I only ever see a 3D shadow. Monoliths hide vaults of exotic materials, and $(item)Void Lattice Ore$() is common here.
Physics aside: in brane-world models only gravity leaks out into the Bulk, which might be why it is so much weaker than the other forces. Standing out here, I believe it.
Slip sideways out of this brane and into the Bulk.$(br2)Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$() from 9 Tesseract Core, 18 Alcubierre Coil, 9 Calabi-Yau Manifold, 9 Neutronium Ingot.
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Brane Shifter$(): Cantor Key, Horizon Diver, Planck Diver

Log, the Bulk, fifth crossing. It is not uniform. There are regions: the open $(thing)Bulk$(), the crystal $(thing)Graviton Reefs$() and the $(thing)Moduli Wastes$().

$(thing)Derelict Stations$() hold salvage and supplies - someone came here before me. $(thing)Collapsed Calabi-Yau Knots$() hang over the Wastes with caches at their hearts. In string theory, Calabi-Yau shapes are the tiny curled-up extra dimensions; these have come uncurled.

The locals:$(li)$(thing)Graviton Wisps$() pull you toward them and crush you up close.$(li)$(thing)Brane Striders$() slip between branes when hurt and leave you seeing double.$(li)$(thing)Moduli Crawlers$() hunt in packs and climb anything.$(br2)I keep my back to a wall. It does not help with the Crawlers.

Ruins and impossible structures keep their treasure in $(item)Containment Caches$(), not chests. Each dimension seals its own kind: the Bulk Cache borrows room from a fifth dimension, the Euclid Reliquary of the Platonic Realm closes on an exact right angle, the Hilbert Locker is always full and always has room for one more.
A cache works like a chest of 27 slots; hoppers and pipes can reach it. Breaking it spills its contents and drops the cache itself. You can make an ordinary $(item)Containment Cache$() of your own.
Sunday. Even a lab deserves some style. Put a block of any high-tech material in a $(item)Stonecutter$() for plating, tiles, bricks and pillars - and back again, so nothing is wasted.

Surround a material block with glowstone dust for four $(item)Lamps$(). Most bricks and tiles also come as stairs, slabs and walls.$(br2)Chronosteel, Spacetime Alloy, Cosmic Neutronium, Dilithium and Void Lattice each have a storage block too - which is how I keep the hoard tidy.
Made in a crafting grid from 4 Glowstone Dust, Block of Cherenkov Quartz.
Nether expedition, day 2. $(item)Dilithium$() grows down here. Its lattice is porous to antimatter, which makes it the only practical regulator for an annihilation reactor.

Field notes: annihilation turns all the rest mass of matter and antimatter into energy - E = mc², the full amount, against under 1% for fusion. The hard part has always been holding antimatter without it touching anything. A crystal it can pass through gently is exactly what such a reactor needs.
Porous to antimatter. It regulates annihilation reactions.$(br2)Made in $(item)Einstein-Rosen Bridge Projector$() from Dilithium Crystal, Sterile Neutrino, 1,000 mB Exotic Matter.

Every other place has its own law, and the law is not kind to visitors. Carry the right $(thing)attunement$() anywhere in your inventory and you will live - with a reminder of where you are.

In the white hole gravity points $(thing)up$() - sneak to fall.$(li)$(item)Identity Kernel$(), the Transcendental: without it, $(thing)Dissolution$().

None of these places has a bottom you can die on. Fall off the floor of one and you fall into another:$(li)off the $(thing)Bulk$(): back onto our own brane$(li)through the $(thing)Platonic Realm$(): into the Transfinite Hierarchy$(li)below the $(thing)Transfinite$(): into the Quantum Foam

$(li)through a $(thing)black hole$()'s singularity: out of its white hole$(li)past the top of a $(thing)white hole$(): home$(li)between the branches of $(thing)Hyperdimensional Reality$(): into the Bulk$(li)out of the $(thing)Transcendental$(): into Hyperdimensional Reality$(br2)Carry the right attunement for wherever you land.
Stand inside a structure built in more dimensions than three and your eyes stop agreeing with your feet. The deeper you go, the more space folds to match the object you are in:

$(li)$(thing)Tesseracts$() and Bulk monoliths: nested cubes turning inside one another$(li)$(thing)Fractals$(): the view contains itself, again and again$(li)$(thing)Platonic solids$(): mirrored through their symmetry$(li)$(thing)Hilbert's Hotel$() and the Ordinal Spire: an endless corridor$(li)$(thing)Calabi-Yau knots$() and Hopf rings: space wound round itself

$(li)$(thing)Graviton reefs$(): light bent into an Einstein ring$(li)$(thing)Anomaly vaults$(): the picture tears$(li)the heart of the $(thing)Transcendental$(): all of it at once.$(br2)It is harmless, and fades as you walk out. It can be switched off in the client config (structureDistortion).

A lamp that shines when its axiom is in force. Its light is steady and colourless, and when the axiom is withdrawn it simply goes dark. Rows of them read like a truth table drawn in light. Watching them, I finally understood how much of mathematics is a matter of choice.
pages.title: Axiom Lamp

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)These lit and darkened as I flipped axiom toggles inside the proof. They showed me which postulates I had accepted, and which I had not.

A switch that adopts or rejects an axiom. Flip it and the local truths rearrange; some things become provable, others not. It moves with a satisfying click, like choosing between Euclidean and hyperbolic geometry.
pages.title: Axiom Toggle

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Inside the proof I found switches wired to the axiom lamps. Each one admitted or denied a single postulate. Solving the room meant choosing a consistent set.

A thread pulled from a brane, the membrane on which strings end. It is strong beyond any material, because its tension is a property of spacetime rather than chemistry. It hums faintly and pulls back toward the surface it came from.
pages.title: Brane Tension Fiber

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Brane Striders walk on membranes in the Bulk, and when they fell they left these threads behind. I found more in derelict stations, still taut as if attached to something invisible.

pages.title: Cherenkov Bricks

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I cut Cherenkov quartz into bricks to make glowing walls with more texture than plain blocks. The light catches along every seam.

A column of Cherenkov quartz that glows along its length with an even blue. Placed at a doorway it reads like a beam of light holding up the lintel. It is cool and faintly humming. Rows of them along a corridor make it feel like walking beneath a reactor pool.
pages.title: Cherenkov Pillar

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Pillars of Cherenkov quartz gave the labs a sense of structure and a little light. They were easy to cut and look better than they have any right to.

A chronosteel panel painted with warning stripes, used to mark doorways, machine edges and anything I do not want to walk into. The stripes look very slightly out of step with each other. Yellow and black on dull metal - a language every lab in every universe seems to share.
pages.title: Chronosteel Hazard Panel

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)After walking into a running time field once, I started marking hazards. Chronosteel panels with stripes were the clearest way to say keep out.

A column of chronosteel, banded and fluted, that carries a load without complaint. It reflects light in a slightly delayed blur and gives a doorway the feel of an engine room. Its bands are spaced at regular intervals, like the ticks on a clock face.
pages.title: Chronosteel Pillar

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Chronosteel pillars were stronger than I needed and looked better than stone. I used them to frame machine halls. They also make a reliable time reference.

Chronosteel rolled into plates and fixed to a block face. Its sheen is cool and slightly blurred, as if the surface had moved a moment before it was seen. It gives a wall a clean, mechanical look. Rivets mark each corner, set in perfectly even rows.
pages.title: Chronosteel Plating

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I had spare chronosteel, so I plated walls with it. The blurred reflections are a side effect of the metal's own clock and I have grown fond of them.
$(thing)Used in$(): Chronosteel Plating Slab, Chronosteel Plating Stairs.

A chronosteel grille that lets air pass between rooms. The slats are angled to keep light out and air moving, and a faint draught always seems to be flowing through it, even when the room is still. The slats never collect dust, though I have never cleaned them.
pages.title: Chronosteel Vent

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Labs full of machines get stuffy. Chronosteel vents were the obvious fix, and they look the part. The slats were angled by trial and error until the hum of the machines dropped.

A pane of metamaterial that bends light around itself, so the glass is nearly invisible from any angle. Only the edges betray it, as a faint distortion in the room. Walking past it, the room behind seems to shift a little too smoothly, like a painted backdrop.
pages.title: Metamaterial Cloaking Glass

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Metamaterials can steer light around an object. I built them into glass to see if I could make a window that vanished, and it nearly did.

A panel of computronium with fine glowing traces running across its face, like a circuit board that is thinking. It is warm and faintly busy to the touch. The traces brighten when someone stands close, then fade once they walk away, as though the panel had finished noticing them.
pages.title: Computronium Panel

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Computronium walls were too warm as solid blocks. Thin panels gave me the look of a working computer without heating the room.

Computronium cut into tiles, each one lit by faint, shifting traces. A floor of them flickers softly, as if computing something about whoever walks across it. Patterns chase each other across the joints between tiles, too fast to follow, and settle into stillness when the room empties.
pages.title: Computronium Tiles

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I tiled a floor with computronium offcuts. It flickers gently underfoot, and I am almost sure it is only decorative. It has never miscounted anything.
$(thing)Used in$(): Computronium Tiles Slab, Computronium Tiles Stairs.

Cosmic neutronium rolled into plating, dark as space with faint pinpricks of light. A wall of it looks like a window onto the night sky that happens to be load-bearing. Running a hand over it feels like touching cold glass, and the lights inside never quite stay still.
pages.title: Cosmic Neutronium Plating

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Plating walls with cosmic neutronium was extravagant, but the effect was worth it. It is the closest thing to a sky I have indoors.

Cosmic neutronium cut into dark tiles that seem to have tiny points of light deep inside them, like stars seen through a deep well. The floor they make feels impossibly solid. The tiny lights drift very slowly if I watch them long enough, like stars wheeling over a night.
pages.title: Cosmic Neutronium Tiles

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I had offcuts of cosmic neutronium and laid them as tiles. The faint lights inside them were a surprise, and I left them as they were.
$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Neutronium Tiles Slab, Cosmic Neutronium Tiles Stairs.

End stone cracked around knots of matter so compressed that its electrons are packed into the lowest states quantum mechanics permits. Pauli exclusion holds it up, not chemistry. The block is far heavier than it looks, and the pick rings against it.
pages.title: Degenerate Matter Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the End, where dead stars seem to have been scattered, a pickaxe bounced off a seam of end stone that was much too heavy. Under the crust was matter pressed into degeneracy, like a fragment of a white dwarf.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the End (mine it for its drop).

In string theory, the dilaton is a field whose value sets the string coupling: how readily strings split and join. This crystal froze one value of it. Hold it up to the light and everything behind it looks slightly more or less substantial.
pages.title: Dilaton Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I found these growing on the Graviton Reefs of the Bulk and inside the Calabi-Yau Knot. Their facets responded to string interactions, and I realised they had frozen the dilaton field in place.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Maxwell's Demon Sorter$() from 128 Bulk Stone, 8 Quantum Dot, 32,000 mB Superfluid Helium.$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Dilaton Ore$(), in veins through the Bulk.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Calabi Yau Knot chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Singularity, String Coupling Crystal.

Pale, oddly variable mineral whose hardness seems to drift as I handle it. The dilaton is the scalar field in string theory that sets the coupling strength of strings; here it is pinned into crystal, and wherever it sits the rules of interaction loosen or tighten slightly.
pages.title: Dilaton Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the bulk stone a seam kept changing how hard my tools struck it. Plotting the variance against depth, I realised the local string coupling was shifting, a frozen dilaton field showing through the rock.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Bulk (mine it for its drop).

Scorched nuggets blown out of a white hole. They are rich in elements that should not exist together, flung up from a region that admits no entry. The surfaces are glassy from the violence of their exit.
pages.title: Ejecta Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The ejecta rock is peppered with dense, blistered lumps. I first took them for meteorites until I traced their trajectories back to a point nothing can enter.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the white hole interior (mine it for its drop).
$(item)Ex Nihilo Engine$().
pages.title: Ex Nihilo Engine

pages.text: A pocket of space sitting in a higher-energy vacuum than its surroundings, metastable and patient. If it tunnels down to the true vacuum it will expand at nearly light speed and rewrite everything it touches. The surface ripples softly, waiting for an excuse.
pages.title: False Vacuum Bubble

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Drifting through the quantum foam, I noticed bubbles whose interior energy did not match the vacuum outside. Coleman's false vacuum, right there. I have learned to give them a very wide berth.

Photons that fell toward a horizon and appear to have stopped. To any outside observer, their final moments are stretched forever, so the ore glows a deep, slow red that never fades. It is not hot, merely luminous and patient.
pages.title: Frozen Light Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Seen from far away, anything falling into a black hole freezes at the horizon. In infall rock I found veins of that frozen light, caught at the instant it crossed and preserved there indefinitely.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the black hole interior (mine it for its drop).

The heart of a Graviton Wisp: a closed loop of string vibrating in the mode that makes a graviton. Even out of the Wisp, it pulls gently on everything nearby. It is light, but holding it gives a faint sensation of falling toward it.
pages.title: Graviton Wisp Core

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Graviton Wisps drift through the Bulk, and when one dissipated it left this behind. I found more in the Calabi-Yau Knot, still faintly attracting dust.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Graviton Condenser$() from 48 Graviton Crystal, 24 Bulk Crystal.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Graviton Wisp.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Calabi Yau Knot chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Graviton Crystal.

Glass held together by a hexagonal force field, like a honeycomb of light. Each cell glows faintly at its edges. It is strong and very slightly warm to the touch. Tapping it makes each hexagon ring separately, a soft chiming that dies away quickly.
pages.title: Hexagonal Field Glass

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I wanted a stronger glass for labs. A hexagonal field pattern spread stress evenly across every cell, and the honeycomb glow came free.

An ender pearl wrapped in bulk stone and cosmic neutronium and charged by a nether star. Thrown, an ordinary pearl takes you somewhere; this one would take you everywhere. It shimmers and is never quite in the place it appears to be.
pages.title: Hyperdimensional Pearl

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Ender pearls teleport through some hidden dimension. Wrapping one in bulk stone gave it access to all of them, and a nether star kept it from scattering on the Extreme Assembly Table.

$(thing)Made$(): Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$() from 48 Bulk Stone, 24 Ender Pearl, 8 Cosmic Neutronium Ingot, Nether Star.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Omniscience Catalyst.

Spheres in four dimensions leave odd traces when they intersect our three. This ore shows them as nested balls that swell and shrink as I turn the lump. It has no corners anywhere and rolls slightly uphill.
pages.title: Hyperspherical Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Slicing a 4-sphere with a 3-dimensional plane gives a growing then shrinking ball. In the ordinal stone I found ore whose cross-sections did exactly that as I rotated it. Something four-dimensional was buried here.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Transfinite Hierarchy (mine it for its drop).

Kaluza and Klein noticed that general relativity in five dimensions, with one dimension curled up small, produces electromagnetism for free. Momentum around that hidden circle appears as electric charge. The shard has a faint static charge and seems to hum slightly when spun.
pages.title: Kaluza-Klein Shard

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I first found these in the Bulk, among Brane Strider remains and derelict stations. Running bulk stone through Maxwell's Demon Sorter with helium, I could separate grains with momentum in the fifth dimension.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Maxwell's Demon Sorter$() from 64 Bulk Stone, 4 Coherent Wiring Harness, 4,000 mB Superfluid Helium.$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Kaluza-Klein Ore$(), in veins through the Bulk.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Brane Strider.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Derelict Station chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Compactification Lathe, Compactified Circle, Dimensional Singularity.
$(thing)Moduli Crawler$(). Lives in: Moduli Wastes, The Bulk.$(br)Drops: Moduli Crystal, Void Lattice Shard.
pages.title: Moduli Crawler

pages.text: The extra dimensions of string theory have shapes and sizes set by fields called moduli. This crystal is those parameters frozen solid: a record of exactly how the hidden dimensions are curled. It changes shape slightly depending on the angle you view it from.
pages.title: Moduli Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Moduli Crawlers in the Moduli Wastes of the Bulk dropped these, and more lay inside the Calabi-Yau Knot. Measuring their facets, I found they recorded the shape and size of the compact dimensions.

$(thing)Made$(): Made in $(item)Maxwell's Demon Sorter$() from 128 Bulk Stone, 8 Quantum Dot, 32,000 mB Superfluid Helium.$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Moduli Ore$(), in veins through the Bulk.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Moduli Crawler.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Calabi Yau Knot chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Dimensional Singularity, G₂ Manifold.

Each crystal here is a snapshot of one possible shape for the hidden dimensions. Moduli are the dials that describe the size and shape of compactified space, and this ore holds those dials fixed in mineral form. Different veins, different geometries, all perfectly valid.
pages.title: Moduli Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)String theory admits an enormous landscape of vacua, each set by its moduli. Mining the bulk, I noticed no two lumps of this ore refract light the same way. Each one has settled into a different vacuum.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Bulk (mine it for its drop).

A column of neutronium with fluted sides, built to carry loads that would buckle any ordinary pillar. It is heavy enough to feel rooted and smooth enough to feel cold. Flat-topped and square-shouldered, it looks like it was designed to outlast the building around it.
pages.title: Neutronium Pillar

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Pillars were a practical need in larger labs. Neutronium columns carried everything I put on them, so I stopped worrying about the ceiling.

Neutronium rolled into flat plates and riveted onto a block face. It is grey, dense and almost reflective, with seams that look as though they were drawn with a ruler. It gives a lab the look of a reactor vault.
pages.title: Neutronium Plating

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I had more neutronium than I needed for machines, so I started plating walls with it. It is overbuilt for decoration, but it never dents.
$(thing)Used in$(): Neutronium Plating Slab, Neutronium Plating Stairs, Neutronium Plating Wall.

Neutronium cut into small square tiles and laid in a grid. The tiles are perfectly flat and very slightly cold, and footsteps on them sound muffled, as if the floor is absorbing more than sound. Each joint is so fine a hair would not fit in it.
pages.title: Neutronium Tiles

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Tiling neutronium was a way to use offcuts from plating. The grid pattern makes the floors of a lab easy to read at a glance.
$(thing)Used in$(): Neutronium Tiles Slab, Neutronium Tiles Stairs.

A plate that collapses whatever stands on it. Step onto it and the surrounding superpositions resolve into definite states. It is smooth, unbreakable, and faintly cold, like an eye that never blinks. Standing on it, I am briefly part of the experiment.
pages.title: Observer Plate

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the proof chambers I noticed certain puzzles changed when I stood on these plates. Observation forced the room into one outcome, a measurement made by standing still.

Ore whose crystals arrive in sequence: each one has a definite successor, and even infinite chains of them have a limit crystal waiting beyond. Breaking a lump never disturbs the order of what remains.
pages.title: Ordinal Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the ordinal stone I found a vein where crystals grew in strict succession, with a larger one capping every infinite run. Von Neumann's construction of the ordinals, rendered in mineral.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Transfinite Hierarchy (mine it for its drop).

Cherenkov quartz polished until its surface is glassy and its glow is even across the whole face. In a dark room it gives off a cool blue light like water around a reactor core. My reflection in it is tinted blue and very slightly brighter than I am.
pages.title: Polished Cherenkov Quartz

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Raw Cherenkov quartz glows unevenly. Polishing the block smoothed the light, and I began using it for walls where I wanted a gentle, cool shine.

Dilithium polished to a mirror finish, its violet colour deep and even. It rings very faintly when touched, and a room of it seems to hum one long note. The surface is clear enough to see my own reflection tinted violet, and fingerprints vanish from it almost as soon as they appear.
pages.title: Polished Dilithium

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Raw dilithium blocks were rough and uneven. Polishing them brought out the colour, and I started using them for walls I wanted to look calm.

The foundation of the proof, the ground everything rests on. Its surface is etched with axioms, plain and unhurried, and nothing built above it can sink through. Walking on it is the closest I come to certainty.
pages.title: Ground of the Proof

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Every proof begins from axioms. Inside this one, those axioms are the floor itself, unbreakable because nothing in the proof can deny them.

A thin, translucent barrier between one stage of the argument and the next. It parts only once the preceding step is established, letting me through like a lemma admitted into the main proof. Pressing a hand to it feels like meeting an objection politely raised.
pages.title: Membrane of the Proof

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I found I could not pass certain sheets inside the proof until I had resolved the puzzle before them. Each one is a membrane, a gate held shut by an unproven step.

Ore that knows when it is going to be mined. The vein grows brighter before my pick arrives, and splinters along lines that only make sense once the strike has happened. Holding it feels like being remembered.
pages.title: Retrocausal Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)White holes run time backwards. Mining the ejecta rock, I noticed this ore cracking a moment before I struck it. The effect preceded the cause, and the cause still happened.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the white hole interior (mine it for its drop).

A tear in the fabric that leads back the way I came. Its edges shimmer in the colours of the home dimension, and the air nearby smells faintly of ordinary rain. It is the one rift I am always glad to see.
pages.title: Return Rift

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)After crossing into a far dimension I found this hovering nearby, a seam that the crossing itself had left behind. Stepping through it brought me home. I now note where each one sits before exploring.

Spacetime alloy bricks stacked in an offset pattern. The wall seems slightly curved even when perfectly straight, and its shadows fall a fraction off where they should. The mortar lines bend gently, like a grid drawn on a stretched sheet, and the effect is strongest at the corners.
pages.title: Spacetime Bricks

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I wanted a spacetime wall with texture, so I cut the alloy into bricks. The wall looks like it is leaning into another dimension, but it is not.
$(thing)Used in$(): Spacetime Bricks Slab, Spacetime Bricks Stairs, Spacetime Bricks Wall.

A panel of spacetime alloy whose surface seems to bend inward slightly, as if the wall behind it were further away than it is. It is cool, smooth and very faintly disorienting to look at for long. Its edges line up neatly in rows.
pages.title: Spacetime Panel

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Spacetime alloy made interesting walls, but solid blocks were too much. Panels gave me the effect without the weight. They are also easy to cut to size.

Spacetime alloy cut into tiles that never quite look square. Each tile bends the space around it a fraction, so the grid seems to ripple gently as I walk across it. Nothing placed on them ever rolls, even though the floor looks curved. The ripple is optical, not physical, which I confirmed with a marble.
pages.title: Spacetime Tiles

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I tiled a floor with spacetime alloy to see what would happen. The floor ripples, but it holds, and I liked it enough to keep it.
$(thing)Used in$(): Spacetime Tiles Slab, Spacetime Tiles Stairs.

A seam of metal pulled thin by gravity gradients. One end of every grain feels a stronger pull than the other, and the ore is threaded with stretch marks. It flexes slightly in the hand, as if still being tugged.
pages.title: Tidal Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Tidal forces are the difference in gravity across an object. Deep in infall rock I found metal that had been stretched rather than crushed, and recognised the signature of a nearby singularity.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the black hole interior (mine it for its drop).

A vein where gravity itself fizzes. The quanta of the gravitational field appear and vanish here so densely that the ore feels slightly heavier one moment and lighter the next. Nearby dust drifts in slow, uneven arcs.
pages.title: Ephemeral Graviton Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)No detector has ever caught a single graviton. Picking through foam substrate, I found a seam where my plumb line twitched in rhythm with bursts of vacuum noise. Borrowed gravitons, pinned in stone.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Quantum Foam (mine it for its drop).

A vein that points only one way. Each fleck carries a lone magnetic pole, north without south or the reverse, which classical electromagnetism forbids. A compass held close swings and holds, refusing to recover.
pages.title: Ephemeral Monopole Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Dirac showed one monopole anywhere would explain why charge is quantised. In foam substrate my compass locked onto a single seam and would not let go: monopole pairs, flickering up from the vacuum.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Quantum Foam (mine it for its drop).

Glints of light that do not come from anywhere. Virtual photons, the messengers that carry the electromagnetic force, wink in and out of this vein, so the ore glows without a source. It is cool to the touch despite the sparkle.
pages.title: Ephemeral Photon Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Every electric force is an exchange of virtual photons. Working in foam substrate I saw a seam lit from within, though nothing nearby could be lighting it. The vacuum was lending light and briefly forgetting to take it back.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Quantum Foam (mine it for its drop).

Quarks borrowed from the vacuum and caught before they could be returned. They glow in shifting red, green and blue, colour charge that never settles, and the vein flickers as pairs pop into being and vanish. Leave it alone and it seems to breathe.
pages.title: Ephemeral Quark Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In foam substrate I saw sparks that lasted only an instant, virtual quark pairs living on borrowed energy. One seam held them a little longer than the uncertainty principle should allow, long enough to mine.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Quantum Foam (mine it for its drop).

Void lattice cut into bricks - rigid blocks of nothing stacked with careful joints. The wall looks like a pattern of very clean holes in the world. Each brick has crisp, flawless edges, and the joints between them are the only part that looks like ordinary matter. Torchlight seems to fall into them.
pages.title: Void Lattice Bricks

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I wanted a wall that looked like empty space with structure. Void lattice bricks were exactly that, and they stack as well as stone.
$(thing)Used in$(): Void Lattice Bricks Slab, Void Lattice Bricks Stairs, Void Lattice Bricks Wall.

Bulk stone holding pockets of a crystal made of nothing - a lattice of empty sites that remains rigid even though there is nothing in them. It looks like a gap in the rock that has decided to be solid.
pages.title: Void Lattice Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Mining in the Bulk, I hit a patch of rock that the pick went through as though it were air but that still dropped something. The lattice was a crystal of vacancies, ordered without anything to order.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Bulk (mine it for its drop).

A column of void lattice, rigid emptiness standing upright. It carries weight without any matter inside it, which still seems wrong every time I look at it. Torchlight passes straight into it and does not come out, so the column reads as a perfectly black stripe standing in the room.
pages.title: Void Lattice Pillar

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I needed pillars in a void-lattice room and cut them from the same material. They hold up the ceiling with nothing at all.

Void lattice cut into flat tiles. A floor of them looks like standing on a grid laid over nothing at all, and it is perfectly solid underfoot. My footsteps make no echo at all, and a dropped tool lands silently, as though the floor were listening too hard to make any sound.
pages.title: Void Lattice Tiles

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I tiled a floor with void lattice to see if it would hold. It held, and looking down at it is an experience I recommend once.
Survey notes. $(item)Cherenkov Quartz$() grows deep in the deepslate layer. $(item)Degenerate Matter$() is found in End stone; smelt or blast it into $(item)Neutronium$().

$(item)Void Lattice$() only forms in the Bulk.$(br2)Names explained: Cherenkov light is the blue glow of particles outrunning light in a medium. Degenerate matter is what remains when atoms are crushed until only quantum exclusion holds them up, as in white dwarfs and neutron stars.
Glows with the blue light of particles outrunning light in a medium.$(br2)Made in $(item)Lattice Growth Vat$() from 16 Quartz, 8 Amethyst Shard, 16,000 mB Water.
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Cherenkov Quartz$(): Block of Cherenkov Quartz, Casimir Plate, Casimir Vacuum Press, Chemical Reactor, Cherenkov Boule and more

Day 9. Found one: a crashed research observatory, its containment dome cracked, a supply cache still inside. They dot the Overworld. Who built them, I don't yet know.$(br2)A good source of early Cherenkov Quartz and Neutronium - worth a detour before I can make either myself.

A cache the Transcendental keeps for itself - and the one you can build: 243 kinds of item, and up to $(thing)2,147,483,647$() of each. Whatever you put in joins the pile of the same item. Scroll to move through its 27 rows; a click or shift-click takes one normal stack at a time.
Pipes put into it and take out of it (one stack at a time). Broken, it keeps everything inside. It is made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
